data.title: PostgreSQL Full-Text Search: Fast When Done Right (Debunking the Slow Myth)
data.author: VoVAllen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Postgres 全文搜索（FTS）的性能、优化及其与其他搜索系统（如Elasticsearch）的对比

不同观点：
• **[retakeming]**：作为pg_search的维护者，认为Postgres文档中同时认可多种优化策略。pg_search的目的是解决如何让Postgres在各种复杂查询（如布尔、模糊、分面、相关性排序等）上达到Elasticsearch级别的性能，而不是针对单一查询的优化。Neon/ParadeDB的基准测试包含12个查询，虽然可以通过创建复合索引等方法优化，但这些方法在实际应用中不现实。pg_search提供了一种简单的索引定义，无需用户对每个文本列进行重复操作。

• **[danpalmer]**：批评了Neon/ParadeDB文章中的基准测试方法，认为其错误在于动态计算tsvector，而Postgres文档中已经明确说明了如何优化查询性能。他认为这种错误要么是故意误导，要么是由于没有仔细阅读文档。

• **[nattaylor]**：关注查询计划（explain plans），提到如果查询使用了索引，那么动态重新检查tsvector只会在匹配项上进行，且由于查询限制了返回10条数据，因此重新检查的数量有限。但如果查询在两个GIN索引上有条件，则可能导致不必要的工作。

• **[nostrebored]**：质疑为什么人们希望把所有功能（如向量搜索、全文搜索、工作负载编排、队列等）都放入Postgres中，不理解这种趋势。

• **[zhousun]**：支持更多“Postgres原生”的全文搜索实现，认为像Lucene/Tantivy这样的解决方案由于设计初衷不同，与Postgres的堆表结合时效果不佳。

• **[some_developer]**：分享了多年前尝试使用Postgres原生FTS失败的经历，由于在插入频繁的表上添加索引导致事务超时，最终不得不放弃。

• **[atemerev]**：认为1000万条记录是一个玩具数据集，建议使用更大的数据集（如完整的维基百科或Reddit评论）来进行基准测试以获得更有意义的比较。

• **[ltbarcly3]**：认为Postgres全文搜索过于僵化，无法进行复杂调优，如子字符串搜索、自定义分词等，而Solr和Elasticsearch在这方面提供了更强的配置能力。Postgres的FTS系统被视为一个简单的玩具系统，无法满足复杂需求。

补充讨论：
• **[chenhoey1211]**：提到很多团队直接选择Elasticsearch或Meilisearch，而忽视了Postgres原生FTS的潜力，并提出SQLite+FTS5+Wasm是否能在浏览器中提供类似的性能表现，作为离线优先应用的方向。

• **[briankelly]**：认为问题不在于速度，而在于规模，建议在系统达到极限之前继续使用。

• **[Thaxll]**：认为定制的Postgres代码不能称之为“原生”。

• **[Sytten]**：认为这种内容营销对于像ParadeDB这样的初创公司来说是一个很好的宣传方式。

争议焦点：
• Postgres FTS的优化方法及其实用性。
• 是否应该将所有功能集成到Postgres中。
• Postgres FTS与其他搜索系统（如Elasticsearch）在灵活性和性能上的比较。

data.title: The Barium Experiment
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GUI工具包的设计、选择以及对现有工具（如GTK、Qt）的评价

不同观点：
• [nine_k] 认为，专注于Xlib且使用Common Lisp编写的GUI工具包（如Barium）因为不考虑兼容性问题，可以更精简高效。同时，对GTK模仿苹果将 scrollbars 隐藏的设计选择表示不满。
• [zombot] 反对被局限于某种特定的生态系统（暗指Gnome/GTK），并认为这种限制代价高昂。
• [rtpg] 认为Qt/KDE在避免Gnome/GTK相关问题上表现更好，但承认Qt本身也比较"笨重"。
• [userbinator] 提到GUI框架的快速变化（churn）迫使开发者不断修改旧代码，并认为Win32 (+WINE) 是一个更稳定的GUI API选择。
• [nsm] 推荐Racket语言的GUI实现，认为其成熟且跨平台，尤其是与GTK集成良好，适用于教学IDE等场景。
• [boxed] 认为NeXTStep仍然领先于大多数现代GUI框架。
• [01HNNWZ0MV43FF] 对重新发明GUI框架表示兴趣，但认为使用非LISP语言绑定到Barium的实际应用可能性不大。
• [jeffbee] 不理解为什么从GTK2迁移到GTK3会被视为灾难，并质疑为何开发者必须被迫跟随这种"变化"。
• [DeathArrow] 认为使用现有GUI框架（如GTK、Qt等）进行开发困难且容易出错，不具备未来可持续性，因此有人选择自己开发工具包，但这往往是出于实验或乐趣。
• [snvzz] 对Barium这样的新工具包表示支持，希望其能够持久发展，而非像其他流行工具包那样迅速膨胀和消亡。
• [duskwuff] 解释GTK等工具包随时间演变的原因，指出Linux桌面环境的变化导致UI库也需要适应新的硬件和需求，认为期望UI库20多年不变是不现实的。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于开发者是否应被"强迫"跟随GUI框架的演变（如GTK2到GTK3的迁移），以及现有框架如GTK和Qt的优缺点。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是不同开发者对稳定性和新颖性的不同追求，一些开发者倾向于选择老旧但稳定的API（如Win32），而另一些开发者则寻求创新和实验性技术（如Barium、Racket）。
• 对图形和单位标注的正确性也有一个小讨论，[yohbho] 指出学术论文中常见的标注错误，反映出对细节的关注。

data.title: DIY experimental reactor harnesses the Birkeland-Eyde process
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个由公民科学家Marb自制的实验反应器，利用Birkeland-Eyde过程通过电弧将空气中的氮转化为硝酸。该过程曾在化肥生产中使用，但由于高能耗在一百年前被淘汰。Marb主要出于对科学的兴趣，使用Arduino UNO Rev3控制反应器，通过 breakout shield 调节电弧电源，并使用传感器监控反应条件。尽管该过程效率不高，Marb的设计重点在于空气干燥和电弧控制。他展示了一次实验演示，并表示如果有足够兴趣，会制作更详细的 follow-up 视频。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过特定技术或设备生成硝酸及其应用的可能性和潜在问题

不同观点：
• **ashoeafoot** 认为是否有必要使用长弧来生成表面，并建议是否可以采用分形表面来实现弧形和隔离效果，可能在质疑当前方法的复杂性或效率。

• **mikewarot** 指出，当能源的边际成本接近零时，效率问题变得不那么重要。这一观点表明，如果使用多余的太阳能，该技术在离网情况下尤其有价值，暗示该方法在特定条件下是可行的。

• **8474_s** 强调该技术的潜在应用，认为它可以实现闭环系统，补充通常需要氮固定的土壤，这表明该技术在农业和生态系统维护方面可能有重要作用。

• **dfedbeef** 提出担忧，认为在YouTube上发布此类操作的详细步骤可能不是个好主意，因为硝酸是某些受到严格监管和危险的物质的前体，暗示可能存在安全隐患或法律问题。

• **NoMoreNicksLeft** 提到YouTube上的Andreas the Alchemist有一个升级版的设备，每天能生产大约一加仑的硝酸，且浓度接近发烟硝酸，但耗电量高达5千瓦时，提供了实际案例来对比效率和产出。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于生成硝酸的步骤公开是否合适，以及该技术在实际应用中的效率和安全性。
• 实际应用中的例子（如Andreas the Alchemist的设备）提供了有关当前技术水平和能耗的重要信息。
• 讨论还涉及到该技术的潜在应用场景，如离网能源利用和农业生态系统维护。

This DIY experimental reactor harnesses the Birkeland-Eyde process
Arduino Team
—
March 17th, 2025
Nitrogen is critical for farming at scale and without some form of nitrogen to enrich the soil, we couldn’t grow staple crops efficiently enough to feed our large global population. Serious science goes into the production of fertilizers and the Birkeland-Eyde process was one early example. It uses electrical arcs to turn nitrogen in the air into nitric acid. Marb is an enthusiastic citizen scientist and built his own experimental reactor to harness the Birkeland-Eyde process.
The Birkeland-Eyde process was largely phased out a century ago, because it is inefficient due to the high energy requirements. It needs a lot of energy to create the electric arcs — too much energy to be practical at the scale necessary for modern industrial farming. But efficiency isn’t a major concern for Marb, who is more interested in the science than fertilizer production.
Creating an electrical arc isn’t very difficult, but controlling it is more challenging. For that reason, Marb used an
Arduino UNO Rev3
to oversee his DIY reactor. Through a breakout shield, the Arduino controls the flow of power to the arc electrodes. That requires a large power supply, transformers, and a boost converter.
The rest of the reactor is devoted to the containment, preparation, and flow of air. The Birkeland-Eyde process works best with dry air, so Marb’s design pumps air through a desiccant-packed tube and into the reaction chamber where the electrodes meet. Sensors, like a temperature sensor, help the Arduino gain feedback on the conditions.
Marb’s video ends with a demonstration, but he hasn’t yet refined the reaction process for maximum yields. If there is enough interest, Marb says that he’ll make a follow-up video with more detail.

data.title: A new way to make graphs more accessible to blind and low-vision readers
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: MIT CSAIL开发了Tactile Vega-Lite系统，简化了触觉图表的设计过程，帮助教育者和设计者高效创建无障碍图表。该工具可以将Excel数据自动转换为视觉图表和触觉图表，内置设计标准，简化了以往需要多种软件配合的复杂流程。通过代码编辑器，用户可以自定义标签、刻度等元素，并利用预设的触觉模式快速调整图表。该工具旨在让不具备触觉设计专长的用户也能轻松创建无障碍图表，特别适用于盲人和低视力读者。这项研究将在2025年的人机交互会议上发表。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：为视障人士提供可触摸图形和学习材料的技术和方法

不同观点：
• [alnwlsn] 分享了自己小时候接触到的一种特殊纸张的经历，这种纸在用马克笔绘画后会产生凸起的效果。他猜测这可能是为盲人设计的可触摸纸张，但之后再也没有遇到过类似材料。
• [froindt] 提到在2011-2014年间参与制作盲人学习材料的经历，描述了当时使用GIMP等工具简化图像并添加盲文的过程，并指出这种手工方法非常耗时。他还分享了团队为表示分子结构开发Blender插件的经验，指出这种复杂方法的准备和实施对普通教育者来说可能过于复杂。
• [lynx97] 提到Tactonom Reader作为一个多模态解决方案，并指出简单的机械解决方案（如特殊纸张和圆珠笔）在过去也行之有效。然而，复杂的数字系统需要更多的准备时间和专业知识，普通教育者可能不愿意或 unable 去使用这些复杂工具。

43595193.article_content:
Breadcrumb
MIT News
A new way to make graphs more accessible to blind and low-vision readers
A new way to make graphs more accessible to blind and low-vision readers
The Tactile Vega-Lite system, developed at MIT CSAIL, streamlines the tactile chart design process; could help educators efficiently create these graphics and aid designers in making precise changes.
Alex Shipps
|
MIT CSAIL
Publication Date
:
March 25, 2025
Press Inquiries
Press Contact
:
Adam
Conner-Simons
Email:
aconner@csail.mit.edu
Phone:
617-324-9135
MIT Computer Science & Artificial Intelligence Lab
Close
Caption
:
The Tactile Vega-Lite system can take data from something like an Excel spreadsheet and turn it into both a standard visual chart and a touch-based one. Design standards are hardwired as default rules within the program, helping educators and designers automatically create accessible tactile charts.
Credits
:
Image: Alex Shipps/MIT CSAIL, with elements from Pixabay.
Previous image
Next image
Bar graphs and other charts provide a simple way to communicate data, but are, by definition, difficult to translate for readers who are blind or low-vision. Designers have developed methods for converting these visuals into “tactile charts,” but guidelines for doing so are extensive (for example, the Braille Authority of North America’s 2022 guidebook is 426 pages long). The process also requires understanding different types of software, as designers often draft their chart in programs like Adobe Illustrator and then translate it into Braille using another application.
Researchers from MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL) have now developed an approach that streamlines the design process for tactile chart designers. Their program, called “Tactile Vega-Lite,” can take data from something like an Excel spreadsheet and turn it into both a standard visual chart and a touch-based one. Design standards are hardwired as default rules within the program to help educators and designers automatically create accessible tactile charts.
The tool could make it easier for blind and low-vision readers to understand many graphics, such as a bar chart comparing minimum wages across states or a line graph tracking countries’ GDPs over time. To bring your designs to the real world, you can tweak your chart in Tactile Vega-Lite and then send its file to a Braille embosser (which prints text as readable dots).
This spring, the researchers will present Tactile Vega-Lite in a
paper
at the Association of Computing Machinery Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems. According to lead author Mengzhu “Katie” Chen SM ’25, the tool strikes a balance between the precision that design professionals want for editing and the efficiency educators need to create tactile charts quickly.
“We interviewed teachers who wanted to make their lessons accessible to blind and low-vision students, and designers experienced in putting together tactile charts,” says Chen, a recent CSAIL affiliate and master's graduate in electrical engineering and computer science and the Program in System Design and Management. “Since their needs differ, we designed a program that’s easy to use, provides instant feedback when you want to make tweaks, and implements accessibility guidelines.”
Data you can feel
The researchers’ program builds off of their 2017 visualization tool
Vega-Lite
by automatically encoding both a flat, standard chart and a tactile one. Senior author and MIT postdoc Jonathan Zong SM ’20, PhD ’24 points out that the program makes intuitive design decisions so users don’t have to.
“Tactile Vega-Lite has smart defaults to ensure proper spacing, layout, and texture and Braille conversion, following best practices to create good touch-based reading experiences,” says Zong, who is also a fellow at the Berkman Klein Center for Internet and Society at Harvard University and an incoming assistant professor at the University of Colorado. “Building on existing guidelines and our interviews with experts, the goal is for teachers or visual designers without a lot of tactile design expertise to quickly convey data in a clear way for tactile readers to explore and understand.”
Tactile Vega-Lite’s code editor allows users to customize axis labels, tick marks, and other elements. Different features within the chart are represented by abstractions — or summaries of a longer body of code — that can be modified. These shortcuts allow you to write brief phrases that tweak the design of your chart. For example, if you want to change how the bars in your graph are filled out, you could change the code in the “Texture” section from “dottedFill” to “verticalFill” to replace small circles with upward lines.
To understand how these abstractions work, the researchers added a gallery of examples. Each one includes a phrase and what change that code leads to. Still, the team is looking to refine Tactile Vega-Lite’s user interface to make it more accessible to users less

data.title: Quality-of-Life in Tetris Games
data.author: juancroldan
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同版本和变种的俄罗斯方块游戏设计及其规则差异

不同观点：
• jchw认为Tetris the Grand Master (TGM) 系列的设计比"guideline"或NES Tetris规则更优雅。他指出TGM的旋转和踢墙规则更简洁，而guideline Tetris的踢墙规则过于复杂且允许一些不合理的操作（如T-Spin Triple）。他还提到TGM的随机生成算法较简单且更具挑战性，而7-bag算法生成块的顺序过于规律，降低了游戏的难度和趣味性。

• downsplat回忆早期DOS版本的俄罗斯方块，并提到他编写的各种变体，包括完全随机生成块的版本和一个总是给出最难块的版本。他更倾向于早期版本的随机性，而非现代的简化随机算法。

• qsort提供了现代Tetris游戏的旋转系统规范链接，并指出"guideline"规则（包括Hold、7-bag、多个预览和易于T-spin的旋转系统）使得多人游戏更加有趣，而不仅是谁能最快地堆叠Tetrises。

• throw10920支持墙踢机制的灵活性，认为当用户尝试进行不允许的操作时，系统应尽量提供接近的有用操作，而不是严格遵守操作语义。

• curiouser3提到Apotris（GBA上的Tetris变体）通过各种设置调整控制和灵敏度，使得游戏体验更加出色。

• jstanley质疑在没有长条块的情况下玩100块的可能性，认为这可能是由于其他bug引起的。

• franze分享了自己制作的非Tetris克隆游戏，并表示仍在研究和改进旋转系统。

• zabzonk回忆早期通过调试器修改游戏的经历，包括去除拷贝保护和添加鼠标支持。

• amichail提到他正在开发的游戏DropZap World，结合了Tetris和Candy Crush的元素，并寻求反馈。

• iNic指出在快速游戏环境中，玩家更喜欢"real"旋转系统而非"NES"旋转系统，因为前者允许用更少的按键放置块。

• isolli询问如何向他的儿子介绍Tetris，并寻找适合的当前游戏版本。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个技术细节，如随机生成算法（7-bag、TGM随机算法）、墙踢机制和旋转系统（SRS）。
• 不同玩家对游戏规则和设计的偏好反映了个人经历和对游戏挑战性的不同期望。
• 争议的焦点在于哪种规则和设计更优越，特别是TGM与guideline Tetris之间的比较。
• 一些评论提到了对早期游戏版本的情感和技术修改，显示了对经典游戏的怀旧和持续探索。

主要讨论点：音频录制设备和麦克风对录音质量的影响

不同观点：
• MrJagil认为音频录制设备对录音质量有重要影响，并提到Zoom F3是新的主力设备，Sony PCM D100则是已停产的经典设备。他表示这些设备在行业内被广泛认可，说明专业人士能够辨别音质好坏。

• kazinator指出，该比较仅针对录音硬件设备，而非麦克风。他提到，虽然有一些使用不同麦克风录制的音频样本，但并没有对麦克风进行量化比较，仅对录音设备进行了定量分析。

• pier25表示，虽然该资源非常有用，但录音中的噪音主要来源于麦克风本身。他以Rode NT1麦克风为例，指出在录制非常安静的音源时，没有听到来自前置放大器的任何噪音。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于录音质量的关键因素。MrJagil强调录音设备的作用，而pier25则认为麦克风对噪音的影响更大。

• kazinator的评论提醒读者注意比较的对象，强调了区分录音设备和麦克风的重要性，以避免混淆两者对音质的影响。

• pier25的实际使用经验为讨论提供了具体的例子，强调了麦克风选择在减少噪音方面的重要性。

data.title: Visual Reasoning Is Coming Soon
data.author: softwaredoug
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了OpenAI最新发布的GPT-4o模型在图像生成和处理方面的突破，特别是其在视觉推理（visual reasoning）上的潜力。过去，多模态大语言模型在处理图像时存在缺陷，模型只能通过文本描述生成图像，导致结果往往与预期不符。而GPT-4o模型能够保留对话的完整上下文，直接生成更一致的图像，解决了这一问题。例如，它可以根据用户提供的猫的照片，准确地给这只猫戴上侦探帽和单片眼镜。

文章还展望了这一技术在实际应用中的广泛可能性，如将手绘图转化为精美的信息图、编辑假期照片、虚拟试衣等。最重要的是，文章预测视觉推理将成为未来的真正创新，模型将能够通过视觉化场景和推理来解决现实问题。文章最后通过一个"杯子中的弹珠"问题演示了视觉推理的潜在应用。

43633568.article_content:
Visual Reasoning is Coming Soon
I gotta say –
I love it living in exponential times
. I can just wish that something existed and then within a month it does! This time it happened with
OpenAI's 4o image generation release
. In this blog post I'll briefly cover the release and why I think it's pretty cool. Then I'll dive into a new opportunity that I think is even more exciting –
visual reasoning
.
Rather watch than read?
Hey, I get it - sometimes you just want to kick back and watch! Check out this quick video where I walk through everything in this post. Same great content, just easier on the eyes!
Why Image Manipulation with LLMs Stinks
Working with images in Multimodal LLMs has been a mostly one-sided affair. On one hand, it's really cool that you can drop an image into an LLM conversation and get the model to reason about it. But when you ask the model to generate an image, there is a disconnect, because all the model can do is describe the image in text and then call out to an external image generation tool to generate the image based on that text. Text is a poor communication medium for images, and the resulting image is often quite disconnected from the expected result because the short description that the LLM provides to the image generation tool will rarely capture the full context of the conversation.
The problem is most pronounced when attempting to go back and forth working on an idea for an image. You can show the LLM an image of your cat and then say "make this cat wear a detective hat and a monocle". The best the model can do is to put a detective hat and monocle on
some
cat, not the one in your image. To make matters worse, the model can't even see the image that it has just created. So if you ask for a modification to first generation attempt, then the subsequent generations are really just starting over from scratch and hoping that a more detailed description to the image generation tool will make things better... it won't.
Left: OpenAI's pet cat. Right: The best a traditional LLM can do when asked to give it a detective hat and monocle.
OpenAI's Release Brings True Image Manipulation to LLMs
OpenAI's image generation release changes all of this. OpenAI's newest GPT-4o model carries the full context of the conversation into the image generation, and rather than call out to an external model, it is the very same GPT-4o model that does the image generation. By carrying the full context of the conversation –
including the previous images
– into the generation of the new image you can generate much more consistent imagery.
Thus, stealing OpenAI's example, you can show it a photo of your cat, tell it to give
your cat
a detective hat, et voila! It works!
Left: OpenAI's pet cat. Right: GPT-4o's generation when asked to give the same cat a detective hat and monocle. Much more consistent!
Now if all we could do with this technology is stick silly costumes on our cats, then this would honestly be a pretty lame achievement. But think about what we're angling for here. You'll be able to turn hand-drawn garbage into sophisticated infographics and marketing material. You'll be able to take crappy matplotlib charts and reformat them as professional-looking plots that go into slides. You'll be able to try on clothes virtually before you buy them. You'll be able to create photo collages from your photos, game assets, and 3D models. You'll be able to edit your vacation photos to remove that one person who blinked. You'll be able to take a photo of your living room and try out different furniture arrangements and color schemes. You'll be able to take a photo of your garden and get suggestions for where to plant new flowers. The possibilities are endless when you can manipulate images with the full context of a conversation.
Visual Reasoning will be the Real Innovation
All of the above is but prologue for what will come next. Models perform better when they take time to reason. This is because models have no internal monologue. Whereas humans pause and think about a question prior to answering, models have to generate tokens in order to think. But to this point models have only been able to reason in the space of words, and words are ill-suited for reasoning through many types of real world problems. But soon the models' new image manipulation capabilities will power a new form of reasoning. Right now, this ability is mostly useful for image editing. Soon, models will have the ability to visualize different scenarios and visually reason about the world around them.
Demoing Visual Reasoning
Let's try out an example right now and get a glimpse of how visual reasoning will work. For our experiment we'll use
Matthew Berman's marble in a cup problem
– it's one of his go-to reasoning challenges when playing around with a new model:
I've put a marble in a glass. The glass is then turned upside down and put on a table. Then the glass is picked up and put into the microwave. Where is the marble?
It's a great problem

data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了如何通过配置PipeWire来改善GPD Pocket 4笔记本电脑扬声器的音质。现代小型扬声器需要大量数字信号处理（DSP）来提升音质，包括低音增强、限制器和根据音量调整的均衡器等技术。文章详细描述了使用Room EQ Wizard软件测量内置扬声器的频率和脉冲响应，并通过生成滤波器曲线来修正不理想的音频特性，特别是约4kHz处的刺耳共振峰。最终，通过PipeWire配置DSP滤波器，显著改善了扬声器的音质。相关代码和配置可在GitHub和AUR上找到。

43635295.article_content:
GPD Pocket 4 Speaker DSP
Configuring PipeWire to make laptop speakers sound better (Bankstown, Convolution/FIR, etc.)
By
Manawyrm (
@manawyrm@chaos.social
)
|
Sunday, April 06, 2025
Result
Motivation
Modern speakers require a lot of DSP magic to sound as good as they do.
Speakers traditionally needed to be built very carefully to achieve a very flat frequency response and as few artifacts as possible.
These days, many mobile devices like phones, laptops, etc. do a lot of digital signal processing in software in order to make tiny speakers output a lot of sound.
Many different tricks are used, such as
psycho-acoustic bass enhancement
, limiters (allowing for higher power peaks) and
volume-dependent equalization
(frequency response of human hearing is very volume-dependent).
The Asahi Linux project (Linux on Apple Silicon MacBooks) has done a lot of work to make MacBooks sound as good as possible on Linux:
AsahiLinux/asahi-audio: Userspace audio for Asahi Linux
How?
Using
Room EQ Wizard
the frequency/impulse response of the built-in speakers was measured.
Even with very suboptimal measurement equipment (cheap microphone, questionable audio interface), we can clearly see the sloped bass response (expected with speakers of this size) and then also a very noticeable peak/resonance at ~4kHz.
This peak is very audible and leads to a harsh, distorted sound when listening to music.
REW can do arithmetic operations on the curves, so after generating a filter curve for a 300Hz slope, both channels were divided (A/B) against that curve and then inverted (1/A) and exported as a .wav impulse response.
That impulse response .wav file can then be used in a convolution DSP filter.
The DSP configuration/pipeline of a 14" MacBook Pro was then used as a template, the multi-speaker setup (modern MacBooks have 6 speakers!) was stripped-down to just a single stereo pair and the parameters were changed a bit.
The impulse response .wav was (of course) replaced with our newly generated REW output.

不同观点：
• skeptrune: 测试了《The Wise Man's Fear》和《Harry Potter》，结果不尽如人意，尤其是角色关系展示不够准确。他更关注如何利用这些图表生成结构化的JSON对象，以改进搜索和推荐功能。
• eterps: 认为如果系统能通过任意epub文件自动生成关系图，而无需完整阅读书籍，将更有趣。建议使用aichat和graphviz实现这一功能。
• rmnclmnt: 测试了《Time Out of Joint》，系统仅正确识别了故事的前半部分，未涉及剧透。
• memhole: 提供链接供用户查看工具的准确性，指出准确率大约在60%左右。
• febed: 利用MermaidJS与LLM结合，成功绘制业务逻辑的流程图，帮助发现了一些极端情况。
• kretaceous: 测试了《Circe》，发现角色关系错误，如将Circe描述为Helios的女儿，但同时又有其他矛盾的关系。
• iddan: 建议将《Pride and Prejudice》加入示例中。

Austen
Austen is an AI-powered Angular application initialized with Analogjs to generate story relationships between book characters using Mermaidjs diagrams.
Features
📚 Search and analyze any book from Open Library
🤖 AI-powered character relationship analysis
📊 Generate Mermaid diagrams
💾 Save, download (SVG, PNG) and manage your generated graphs
🌐 Share graphs publicly or keep them private
🔍 Discover public graphs generated by other users
Example Graph
A character relationship graph generated for "The Wizard of Oz" by "L. Frank Baum":

init: {
'theme': 'base',
'themeVariables': {
'primaryColor': '#BB2528',
'primaryTextColor': '#fff',
'primaryBorderColor': '#7C0000',
'lineColor': '#F8B229',
'secondaryColor': '#006100',
'tertiaryColor': '#fff'
}
}
}%%

data.title: Doing the Prospero-Challenge in RPython
data.author: tekknolagi
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了作者参与的Prospero挑战，该挑战要求渲染莎士比亚《暴风雨》中的一段引文，输入是一个包含7866个操作的数学公式，每个像素都需要评估该公式。作者尝试了多种方法来加速执行，包括添加窥孔优化和实现"仅保留结果符号"的优化，后者效果显著。

作者首先实现了一个简单的SSA形式解释器，作为基准。该解释器将操作名和索引对应，避免运行时字典查找，并按顺序执行操作。然而，这种方法非常慢，因为需要执行大量的浮点运算。

为了优化，作者借鉴了Matt的quadtree方法，通过递归地将图像分成四个象限，并对每个象限进行范围分析，从而显著缩小公式规模。经过几层递归后，公式往往只剩下几百甚至几十个操作，大大提升了渲染速度。

最终，作者在RPython中进行原型设计，并为了性能提升用C重写了程序。所有代码已发布在Github上。

43633457.article_content:
Recently I had a lot of fun playing with the
Prospero
Challenge
by
Matt
Keeter
. The challenge is to render a 1024x1024 image of
a quote from The Tempest by Shakespeare. The input is a mathematical formula
with 7866 operations, which is evaluated once per pixel.
What made the challenge particularly enticing for me personally was the fact
that the formula is basically a trace in
SSA-form
– a
linear sequence of operations, where every variable is assigned exactly once.
The challenge is to evaluate the formula as fast as possible. I tried a number
of ideas how to speed up execution and will talk about them in this somewhat
meandering post. Most of it follows Matt's implementation
Fidget
very closely. There are two points
of difference:
I tried to add more peephole optimizations, but they didn't end up helping
much.
I implemented a "demanded information" optimization that removes a lot of
operations by only keeping the sign of the result. This optimization ended up
being useful.
Most of the prototyping in this post was done in RPython (a statically typable
subset of Python2, that can be compiled to C), but I later rewrote the program
in C to get better performance. All the code
can be found on
Github
.
Input program
¶
The input program is a sequence of operations, like this:
_0
const
2.95
_1
var
-
x
_2

8.13008
_3

_1

3.675

_5
_3
_7
neg
_6
_8
max
_4
_7
...
The first column is the name of the result variable, the second column is the
operation, and the rest are the arguments to the operation.
var-x
is a
special operation that returns the x-coordinate of the pixel being rendered,
and equivalently for
var-y
the y-coordinate. The sign of the result gives the
color of the pixel, the absolute value is not important.
A baseline interpreter
¶
To run the program, I first parse them and replace the register names with
indexes, to avoid any dictionary lookups at runtime.
Then I implemented a simple interpreter for the SSA-form
input program. The interpreter is a simple register machine, where every
operation is executed in order. The result of the operation is stored into a
list of results, and the next operation is executed. This was the slow baseline
implementation of the interpreter but it's very useful to compare against the optimized
versions.

Running the naive interpreter on the prospero image file is super slow, since
it performs 7866 * 1024 * 1024 float operations, plus the interpretation overhead.
Using Quadtrees to render the picture
¶
The approach that Matt describes in his really excellent
talk
is to use
quadtrees
: recursively subdivide the
image into quadrants, and evaluate the formula in each quadrant. For every
quadrant you can simplify the formula by doing a range analysis. After a few
recursion steps, the formula becomes significantly smaller, often only a few
hundred or a few dozen operations.

analysis reveals that the sign for all pixels is determined, then you can fill

data.title: Show HN: Fermi – A Wordle-style game for order-of-magnitude thinking
data.author: andrewrn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个基于费米估算的游戏设计及其用户界面和用户体验问题

不同观点：
• [beeftime] 认为需要手动选择和调整因素，而不是默认提供所有因素。建议像Wordle一样有锁定赢/输状态，并允许增加/减少因素的量级和运算顺序。对当前滑块默认设置导致胜利表示不满。
• [jy14898] 质疑因素的可排序性和可选择性，指出乘法交换律（axb = bxa），并怀疑因素选择的合理性。
• [thatnerd] 指出单位错误，建议增加单位取消检查功能，并希望在方程中选择乘法或除法。
• [zamadatix] 建议增加“普通”和“困难”模式，普通模式提供因素名称，困难模式需要自己提出因素名称和值。提出赢的条件和“超级”赢的建议。
• [bangaladore] 对游戏机制感到困惑，建议默认包含所有因素，并允许减少使用因素。对猜测后的反馈不清表示不满，希望有更明确的提示和比较信息。
• [iterance] 对游戏中的范围和量级问题提出疑问，指出费米问题的目标是达到合适的量级，而非游戏中提供的预设范围。
• [hallh] 认为游戏有潜力但需要打磨，对因素的明显性和滑块的范围限制表示失望，建议更多不相关因素的估算。
• [whiterook6] 在手机上遇到界面问题，无法理解如何选择和操作因素及滑块，整体用户体验混乱。
• [crmi] 喜欢概念但认为UI confusing，建议不提供预设范围以增加难度，并提出逐步提示和分享结果的建议。
• [mncharity] 强调界限而非点估计，建议多重推理链和自我评估机制，以提升费米估算的游戏性。
• [bobdigit] 建议开发针对儿童/年轻观众的版本。
• [mNovak] 认为滑块范围太窄，失去费米估算的乐趣，建议更宽的量级范围和粗略的估算方式。
• [mrngm] 建议简化初始教程，直接展示问题，调整滑块以适应量级思维，并提出多种滑块策略和用户选择方案。

补充讨论：
• 游戏的核心争议在于滑块的默认设置和范围，以及是否应该提供所有因素。部分玩家认为默认设置和预设范围降低了游戏的挑战性和趣味性。
• 用户界面的复杂性和不明确的反馈机制是另一个主要问题，许多玩家在操作和理解游戏机制上遇到了困难。
• 多种模式和不同难度级别的建议被提出，以增加游戏的深度和可玩性。
• 一些玩家对单位错误和缺乏明确的单位取消检查功能表示不满，希望有更严谨的数学机制。
• 总体而言，玩家对游戏的概念表示认可，但对其执行和用户体验方面提出了诸多改进建议。

data.title: Show HN: Comparing product rankings by OpenAI, Anthropic, and Perplexity
data.author: the1024
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成产品排名的有效性和实用性

不同观点：
• AvAn12认为，人类基于特定需求的排名更有意义，AI的单一维度排名会丢失很多信息，尤其是在个性化需求（如选择电吉他）时，AI无法捕捉用户的特殊偏好。
• joshdavham对排名的定义和标准提出疑问，指出某些搜索结果（如“死亡方式”）的排名标准不明确，导致排名的实际意义存疑。
• crowcroft提到在处理品牌和产品时，AI容易混淆不同品牌，尤其是当公司对品牌的区分不明确时，例如在会计软件的排名中出现不同版本的Quickbooks。
• g42gregory对AI的某些排名结果（如AI IDEs中的GitHub Copilot总是排名第一）表示质疑，但对其他类别（如可信新闻来源）则持保留态度。
• albertgoeswoof讨论了AI取代传统搜索引擎的可能性，并关注这种转变对内容生成和排名的影响，特别是市场营销和内容优化的未来。

补充讨论：
• imcritic指出AI在特定技术问题（如“DevOps中的队列系统”）上表现不一致，不同LLM的返回结果存在差异。
• vitorgrs和bluesnews对比了不同LLM（如Anthropic和Gemini）在新闻来源排名上的结果差异。
• tbarbugli提到在搜索具体产品（如跑鞋）时，结果混合了品牌和型号，缺乏一致性。
• lm28469对AI排名的真实性和可信度提出严重质疑，认为结果可能是基于付费或虚假评论，且搜索预测存在不良建议。
• mvdtnz认为AI在产品排名任务上表现不佳，特别是未考虑价格等重要因素，导致结果缺乏实际比较意义。
• thot_experiment基于自己的专业知识批评了AI的排名结果，认为其与现实脱节，主要受市场营销支出影响。
• pencilcode和klysm预测品牌会开始操控AI排名，导致结果质量下降（“enshitification”），并担心Google等传统搜索引擎会因此受损。
• KuriousCat对具体模型（如Perplexity使用的模型）表示好奇，关注技术实现细节。

争议焦点：
• AI生成排名的信息丢失和个性化需求满足不足。
• 排名标准不透明和结果不一致。
• AI在产品和品牌区分上的混淆。
• AI排名受市场营销和付费内容影响的程度。
• AI取代传统搜索引擎的未来影响和潜在问题。

data.title: Vit D supplementation to prevent acute resp infections: review and meta-analysis
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：维生素D补充剂对急性呼吸道感染（ARI）及总体健康的影响

不同观点：
• [seizethecheese] 认为根据荟萃分析，维生素D与安慰剂相比在降低总体ARI风险方面没有统计学上的显著影响，因为p值略微超过0.05的显著性水平。因此，声称维生素D有效预防ARI没有足够支持。
• [brokegrammer] 支持上述观点，明确指出该研究结论是维生素D补充剂无助于预防急性呼吸道感染。
• [johnisgood] 提到尽管有阳光暴露或补充维生素D，维生素D缺乏仍然可能存在，建议进行检测以确保维生素D水平正常。同时分享了个人补充维生素D的经历。
• [normalaccess] 引用了Steve Gibson和Dr. John Campbell的资源，强调了维生素D代谢产物（如calcifediol）在感染后治疗中的潜在作用，而非单纯依赖维生素D补充剂。
• [bmacho] 提出疑问，既然低维生素D水平与流感相关，但补充维生素D没有帮助，是否意味着有其他因素在起作用。
• [rwbt] 关注自然饮食中富含维生素D的食物，除了补充剂外，询问其他获取维生素D的途径。
• [mrandish] 提供了一个综合观点，认为补充维生素D对预防上呼吸道感染效果不明显，但维生素D缺乏可能与感染的严重程度有关。补充维生素D在缺乏时是有意义的，但过量补充可能有害。

补充讨论：
• [gnabgib] 提供了一些相关讨论的链接，涉及到高剂量维生素D对多发性硬化症和COVID-19的影响，但这些讨论在当前评论中没有详细展开。
• [moltar] 推荐使用dminder应用来监测维生素D的摄入量，包括阳光和补充剂的来源。

争议焦点：
• 维生素D补充剂是否能有效预防急性呼吸道感染。
• 维生素D缺乏与感染严重程度之间的关系是否足以支持普遍补充维生素D。
• 补充维生素D的最佳时机和剂量，以及过量补充的潜在风险。

总结：讨论围绕维生素D补充剂在预防和治疗呼吸道感染中的作用展开，不同观点集中在维生素D的效果、缺乏的检测与补充、以及过量补充的风险。讨论还涉及到维生素D代谢产物在感染治疗中的潜在重要性。

data.title: The Mutable OS: Why Isn't Windows Immutable in 2025?
data.author: ndegruchy
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了将Windows操作系统变为不可变系统的可能性和优势。不可变系统意味着操作系统是只读的，无法随意更改，确保系统稳定性。这种设计类似于早期的DeepFreeze软件，但更进一步。不可变系统通过整体替换系统镜像来更新，避免了部分更新失败或不兼容的问题。如果更新失败，系统会自动回滚到上一个正常状态。这种方法已经在macOS等系统中应用，降低了安全风险，并确保系统启动时的完整性。对于Windows来说，实现这种机制需要解决向后兼容性和配置管理的问题，但已有虚拟化和容器技术作为基础。这种设计不仅适用于操作系统，还可以应用于应用程序，确保其安装和运行的稳定性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：操作系统中的不可变性和安全性机制

不同观点：
• [cedws] 认为Windows通过UFW（统一写入过滤器）实现了某种程度的不可变性。他提到可以通过基于RAM或磁盘的覆盖层来处理C盘分区，所有写入操作都会在该覆盖层中进行，并且可以被清除。不过，必须排除某些特定的路径，否则系统会出现问题。此外，覆盖层需要在sysprep阶段之后设置。

• [emchammer] 认为一个操作系统应该是自我托管的，即应该能够在同一台机器上编译和重新安装操作系统。他指出Windows和macOS由于是闭源的，无法实现这一点，并表示如果可以的话，他会选择这样做。

• [ndegruchy] 作为桌面技术支持人员，认为尽管操作系统安全性已经取得了很大进展，但不可变性仍然被视为一种异类。他对此感到不解，并希望听取其他人对这一问题的看法和反面观点。

43633195.article_content:
Today, I’d like to talk about Windows.
Wait, before you go, just hear me out: “What if Windows was an immutable OS?”
This idea might seem familiar to you. We actually had this, for some values of
’this’, back in the aughts. We called it
DeepFreeze
. Of course, it was more
about freezing the whole partition, and less of making the OS itself immutable,
but it was on the right path. Oh, but I haven’t explained “Immutable”.
What?
Immutable, at least as far as software goes, means to be unchanging. If you have
an immutable OS, then the OS is essentially read-only. You can’t make changes,
you can’t fiddle with it, and that’s by design. This doesn’t mean you
can’t
fiddle with it. Projects like Fedora Silverblue and NixOS allow you to fiddle
with the OS, just outside of the running context. Changes come in signed and
sealed updates to the
whole
system, not one-off patches. That means when you
boot your computer, the OS either works, or it doesn’t. If it doesn’t, then most
of these systems will roll back to the last working copy, with no leftover bits
or half-upgraded components. That means you have a solid foundation upon which
to work on.
In short: The system image is a fixed unit. It is what it is at install/update
time. When it comes time to patch, you just replace it, wholesale. If that fails
for whatever reason, the change doesn’t take place and you’re back to where you
were: Working.
We even do this already in the wild with applications. Flatpak, while I disagree
with it being a replacement for good package management, does this for applications.
Microsoft has it’s MSIX apps from the Windows Store and Apple’s built-in apps are
all contained on special partitions that get updated wholesale.
A Brief History
Culture around Operating Systems has evolved over the ~60 years of computing. In
the early days, MS-DOS was just some files on the disk that if you deleted or
modified would kill your system and require an expensive call to a tech. Later,
we organized those files and told people to stay out, but this was mostly
convention and not a hard and fast rule. OSes of the Unix variety did have
permissions to stop tampering, but these were pretty rudimentary and easy to
mess up.
As OSes have matured as the state of the industry has seen more harmful actors
willing data destruction or theft on users and organizations, we’ve put up more
roadblocks. Windows has mostly kept apace with this by erecting stronger
permission models and adding things like UAC and sandboxing with MSIX. Not all
of this is well received, but it’s the state of the system. However, a lot of
the problems that I, as a desktop support tech, see could probably be mitigated
by making the OS layer read-only.
Why?
When your OS is read-only. You, nor Bob, or Sally or xXx420BlazeItBigBallsxXx
can make changes to the system. That’s it. No more weird OS errors, trojans,
unbootable systems, half installed patches or corrupt system files. Your
computer turns on, and verifies the system is the way it’s supposed to be and
you go on your merry way. This allows folks like me and my security “friends” to
worry about your
data
more, and less about tweaking knobs so that you can’t
install 30 toolbars, delete
system32.dll
or get some drive-by-malware
infection from a advertisement.
The patching story cannot be undersold. When “Patch Tuesday” rolls around, you
don’t have to worry about it not finishing and leaving you in a half-working
state, or not applying
some
of the patches because of an improper order or
some weird lock on a file not being removed. The whole thing is replaced. If
that replacement doesn’t work, then you just reboot (probably being done anyway)
and you’re back to the last known good state.
This is being done already on macOS and lowers the effective surface area for
attacks to take root, and makes sure when you turn on your computer, it actually
turns on and boots up. The same system can also be used to ensure that applications
follow the same behavior. Installing Microsoft Office like this would ensure that
when you open Word, Word is what you get. Just like the OS, no more half-installed
configurations, broken components and reinstall/repair cycles to fix that toolbar
button.
How?
Well, that’s the billion-dollar question. There is some groundwork done for this
already. There is virtualization and container support in Windows and we already
have a lot of prior art in Faronics’ DeepFreeze software. The big missing area,
at least as I can see it is backwards-compatibility and handling overrides or
configurations.
The story doesn’t end with monoliths like Microsoft, Apple or Red Hat handing
off blessed OS images and you’re just forced to accept it. You can configure
things, make changes, and deploy images that are blessed. This even allows you
to layer configurations atop a blessed image to further customize it. Keeping
the OS layer pristine, the configurations in their own space and the user system
all separate, but perceptually unified components tha
43633195.article_summary: 本文讨论了将Windows操作系统变为不可变系统的可能性和优势。不可变系统意味着操作系统是只读的，无法随意更改，确保系统稳定性。这种设计类似于早期的DeepFreeze软件，但更进一步。不可变系统通过整体替换系统镜像来更新，避免了部分更新失败或不兼容的问题。如果更新失败，系统会自动回滚到上一个正常状态。这种方法已经在macOS等系统中应用，降低了安全风险，并确保系统启动时的完整性。对于Windows来说，实现这种机制需要解决向后兼容性和配置管理的问题，但已有虚拟化和容器技术作为基础。这种设计不仅适用于操作系统，还可以应用于应用程序，确保其安装和运行的稳定性。

data.title: Baking the Y Combinator from Scratch
data.author: mprast
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了Y组合子（Y Combinator），一个在函数式编程中用于实现递归的数学构造。作者强调不仅要理解“是什么”，还要理解“如何实现”和“为什么重要”。Y组合子用于在不允许显式自引用的函数式语言中实现递归。其定义为：

$$ Y = \lambda f. \enspace (\lambda x. \enspace f(x \enspace x)) \enspace (\lambda x. \enspace f(x \enspace x)) $$

文章分为两部分，第一部分解释Y组合子的构造及其如何产生固定点（fixed point），第二部分讨论其在递归中的应用。Y组合子由逻辑学家Haskell Curry提出，也被称为“固定点组合子”（Fixpoint Combinator）或“悖论组合子”（Paradoxical Combinator）。

Lambda演算中的一切都是函数，没有函数名，所有函数都是匿名函数。固定点是指对函数$f$，存在一个点$x$使得$f(x) = x$。Y组合子是一个固定点组合子，它接受一个单参数函数并返回该函数的一个固定点，满足$Y(f) = f(Y(f))$。

简言之，Y组合子通过实现固定点来支持递归，是函数式编程中一个重要工具。

43636230.article_content:
It's a pedagogical pet peeve of mine when technical concepts are simply listed in their fully developed state, with little in the way of motivation, derivation, or historical context. This, I think, is like publishing a cookbook filled with beautiful pictures of cakes, but no recipes.
My aim with the "Baking <x> from scratch" series is to describe not only
what
, but
how
and
why
, with the hope that this will lead to a richer and more durable understanding.
The Famous Y combinator
This post is about the Y combinator. Not Y Combinator the accelerator, but the mathematical construct that it's named after -
the
Y combinator.
The Y combinator looks like this:
$$ Y = \lambda f. \enspace (\lambda x. \enspace f(x \enspace x)) \enspace (\lambda x. \enspace f(x \enspace x)) $$
Confronted with this definition, you might ask yourself:
Why does it look like that?
What is it used for?
Why do people still talk about it?
(What the heck is a combinator?)
The one-line answer to all of these is: "the Y combinator implements recursion in functional languages that don't allow for explicit self-reference", but it's worth going a little deeper than that. In my opinion, the easiest way to understand what the Y combinator
is
, at a fundamental level, is to focus on how it produces fixed points. The easiest way to understand why it's
important
is to focus on how it can be used to implement recursion. In Part 1 we'll do the former (answering 1. and half of 2. in the process) and in Part 2 we'll do the latter (answering 3. and the other half of 2.)
(We'll answer bonus question 4 later in this article!)
The Y combinator was devised by Haskell Curry, an influential logician who has the unique distinction of lending his name to both a
programming technique
and a
programming language
. It is also known as the "Fixpoint Combinator" (for reasons we'll soon discuss) and the "Paradoxical Combinator" (for reasons we'll investigate in the second half of this post.)
The Lambda Calculus
This post presumes that you're at least familiar with the lambda calculus - you don't have to be an expert, but if it's completely new to you you may have some trouble knowing what's going on.
This
is a good introduction if you need it (this article only draws on the material in Section 1.)
Two things about the lambda calculus that you should understand before reading this:
1)
everything
in the lambda calculus is a function (I'll also call these functions 'terms'.) When you "run" a program in the lambda calculus, you're basically plugging functions into other functions over and over until you can't do it anymore. This may seem like it severely limits the expressive power of the lambda calculus, but consider that we can encode different kinds of data and operators in the lambda calculus by representing them using suitable functions (the linked paper shows how to represent booleans and natural numbers in the lambda calculus, and demonstrates how to do arithmetic and some boolean algebra.) The lambda calculus is Turing Complete, so using this type of encoding you can replicate the behavior of any program written in any language.
2) There are no names besides variable names in the lambda calculus. You can't assign a name to a function and you can't call any functions by name. For the sake of readability I'll sometimes cheat and give a name to a function just to make it easier to explain. For example, I might write
$$id = \lambda x. x$$
and then later:
$$myCoolTerm = \lambda x. x \enspace id(x)$$
Just remember that you technically can't do \(name = term\) or \(name(argument)\) in the real lambda calculus; you have to write everything out. For example, \(myCoolTerm\) can only legally be written as:
$$ \lambda x. x \enspace ((\lambda x. x) (x)) $$
Y - the Fixpoint Combinator
A fixed point (or fixpoint) of a function \(f\) is a point that doesn't change when you apply \(f\) to it. In other words, \(x\) is a fixpoint of \(f\) if and only if
$$f(x) = x$$
Y is a
fixpoint
combinator
(notice I didn't say
the
fixpoint combinator - the Y combinator is one of the oldest and simplest fixpoint combinators, but there are many others!) A fixpoint combinator takes a (one-argument) function and returns some fixpoint of that function (some functions have more than one fixpoint - consider, for example, that every
value returned by an idempotent function is a fixpoint! If the function has
no
fixpoints \(Y(f)\) doesn't terminate.) So we know Y must satisfy:
$$ f(Y(f)) = Y(f)$$
but that also means:
$$Y(f) = f(Y(f))$$
From a computational perspective, this second equation says that the action of \(Y\) is to take a function and
nest itself
in a call to that function.
Because the two equations above are equivalent, finding a \(Y(f)\) that satisfies the second equation means that -
by definition
- \(Y(f)\) is a fixed point of \(f\).
Now is a good time to remember that everything in the lambda calculus is a function. So \(Y\) is a function that takes another function \(f\) and returns a fixed-p

data.title: Show HN: Aqua Voice 2 – Fast Voice Input for Mac and Windows
data.author: the_king
data.article_summary: Aqua Voice是一款先进的语音转文本系统，采用融合转录架构和客户端上下文引擎，能够自动格式化文本以适应不同应用，支持技术提示等新功能。其行业领先的低延迟和快速响应时间，比竞争对手快31%。它适用于Windows和Mac，无需特定应用插件，支持现有工作流。Aqua通过屏幕上下文提升准确性，特别在编码、消息和文档编辑方面表现优异，错误率远低于其他语音输入工具。Aqua提供简单透明的定价方案，包括免费的起步计划和多种付费选项，以满足不同用户需求。

data.title: Show HN: Obelisk – a WASM-based deterministic workflow engine
data.author: tomasol
data.article_summary: Obelisk是一个简单、弹性且安全的工作流引擎，采用单进程运行时和SQLite数据库，无需复杂基础设施。它基于WebAssembly（WASM）构建，支持组件模型，实现确定性工作流执行、隔离和安全性。工作流使用真实代码编写，支持结构化并发，简化了错误处理和清理。引擎具有崩溃恢复和重放能力，所有执行参数和步骤结果都存储在执行日志中，并在超时或失败时重试。它还支持通过Webhook、CLI、gRPC或Web UI触发工作流，且为开源项目，使用Rust编写，遵循AGPL协议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WASM（WebAssembly）在音频效果、工作流引擎、嵌入式系统以及开源许可方面的应用和挑战

不同观点：
• [chaosprint] 提出将WASM用于音频效果和音乐制作，并关注异步处理在WIT（WebAssembly Interface Types）中的实现情况。这表明对WASM在音频处理领域的潜力有积极预期，同时关注具体技术细节（如异步处理）的现状。

• [emgeee] 质疑WASM相对于其他执行引擎的优势，特别是针对短时任务（如500毫秒超时的lambda函数）。他还提出了WASM在嵌入式系统中可能的应用场景，暗示WASM在这些特定环境中的价值可能更高。

• [SvenL] 关心工作流引擎的更新问题，提出了两个具体场景：在有运行实例的情况下是否可以更新工作流，以及是否可以更新运行实例以修复缺陷。如果不能，是否可以通过使用旧版本日志重放更新后的工作流版本。这反映了在实际使用中对工作流引擎维护和升级的实际需求。

• [disintegrator] 对项目的AGPL许可表示关注，认为这可能会影响项目的采用率，除非提供付费许可选项。他还提到自己在设置WASM/WASI以处理HTTP请求时遇到困难，暗示技术门槛可能影响使用体验。

• [Philpax] 提到另一个类似的技术栈实现（https://flawless.dev/），并表示希望了解其与当前项目的区别和关键差异。这表明在技术社区中存在对相似项目进行比较和选择的需求。

补充讨论：
• 关于WASM的应用场景，讨论中提到了音频处理、工作流引擎、嵌入式系统等多个领域，显示出WASM技术的多功能性和广泛兴趣。
• 许可问题被提出作为一个潜在的采用障碍，尤其是在开源社区中，如何平衡技术开放性和商业可行性是一个值得注意的议题。
• 技术实现细节（如异步处理、HTTP请求设置）和实际使用中的维护问题（如工作流更新）也是讨论的重点，显示出用户在实际应用中面临的具体挑战。

争议焦点：
• WASM相对于其他执行引擎的优势在不同应用场景中可能存在不同看法，特别是在短时任务和嵌入式系统中的价值。
• 项目的AGPL许可被认为可能影响采用率，这涉及到开源项目如何在技术开放和商业模式之间找到平衡。

data.title: Photographs of 19th Century Japan
data.author: merothwell
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对日本旧照片的分析与文化变迁的讨论

不同观点：
• canpan：认为一些地点如Kameido Shrine、Osaka Castle等仍然存在，但感叹传统村庄和城镇景象已不复存在，现代房屋大多缺乏特色，直到最近才有人开始重新建造漂亮的房屋。
• hoseyor：将旧照片的消失与全球化导致的独特文化丧失联系起来，批评全球化在摧毁多样性。
• voidUpdate：对僧侣服饰颜色的变化感到好奇，询问是否与等级有关。
• xandrius：喜欢通过旧照片或科幻作品重新体验和理解过去的世界，认为这有助于理解当今文化。
• decimalenough：指出Toshogu Shrine周围的风景变化不大，但像Kobe和Nagasaki这样的城市已完全变样。
• kappasan：提到自己的工作场所是京都一座百年历史的町屋，虽然生活方式有所不同，但仍有历史感。
• potato3732842：感叹有些人在封建日本长大却活到了20世纪50年代，见证了巨大的进步。
• NKosmatos：希望有些旧照片能有现代的对比照片，特别是那些仍然存在的地方。
• throwup238：提到俄罗斯帝国的彩色照片是通过特殊技术制作的，并提供了相关资源的链接。
• userbinator：澄清这些照片不是真实的彩色照片，而是手工上色的。

补充讨论：
• informal007：认为这些照片像人工绘制的画作，而非相机拍摄的照片。
• helaoban：对世界的变化感到惋惜。
• low_tech_punk：对特定照片标题为“Thief, outside of mosquito-net.”感到兴趣。
• RataNova：认为看到那个时代真实的人很有意义。
• tkgally：分享了一些关于那个时期的书面记录链接，提供进一步阅读资料。

争议焦点：
• 全球化对文化多样性的影响是讨论中的一个争议点，hoseyor批评全球化在摧毁文化多样性，而其他人则关注具体地点和文化的变迁。

这些观点共同构成了对日本旧照片及其反映的文化变迁的多元化讨论。

data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种利用豆蔻口香糖（由豆类*Lablab purpureus*制成）对抗病毒的创新方法。这种口香糖含有一种天然抗病毒蛋白（FRIL），能够有效中和疱疹病毒（HSV-1和HSV-2）以及两种流感A病毒株（H1N1和H3N2），减少病毒载量超过95%。该研究由宾夕法尼亚大学牙医学院的Henry Daniell教授及其团队进行，口香糖已符合FDA药物标准，安全性得到验证。研究人员还计划使用豆粉对抗禽流感（如H5N1），试图通过加入鸟饲料控制病毒传播。这项研究为减少病毒感染和传播提供了新的思路，尤其在应对全球健康挑战方面具有重要意义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对病毒感染和免疫的科学讨论，包括特定免疫机制、HPV检测与疫苗、抗病毒药物等话题。

不同观点：
• [hirenj] 认为通过结合病毒包膜上的复杂N-糖链来实现免疫反应，可能缺乏特异性，但鉴于粘膜中N-糖链相对较少，可能仍会击中目标。该评论对机制的有效性和特异性提出质疑。
• [rickydroll] 提出牙科医学不应与其他现代医学实践分离，强调身体各系统的相互关联性，暗示口腔健康与整体健康密切相关。
• [sys32768] 分享了个人经历，未接种HPV疫苗且年龄已大，通过自费测试排除了HPV感染的可能性，但对测试结果的解读存在不确定性，反映了对HPV感染状态的困惑。
• [intrasight] 提到抗病毒药物伐昔洛韦（valacyclovir）可能在减缓痴呆症方面有作用，并计划与医生讨论开始使用该药物。该评论引入了与病毒相关但侧重于神经系统疾病的讨论。
• [djrj477dhsnv] 对没有商业化产品利用唾液中的抗病毒机制表示惊讶，并建议是否可以改进以保护身体其他部位，提出了技术应用的扩展可能性。
• [interludead] 认为针对口腔的病毒传播途径开发防护手段是显而易见的策略，但对目前缺乏此类常见手段表示不解。
• [frankus] 对视频中使用狗（或狼人）口腔模型表示好奇，属于对展示方式的非技术性质疑。
• [sitkack] 强调所有人都应接种HPV疫苗，不论年龄和性别，提供了多个权威来源支持这一观点，明确支持HPV疫苗的广泛接种。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是HPV疫苗的接种范围和年龄限制，[sys32768] 的个人经历与 [sitkack] 的广泛接种建议形成对比。
• 另一个讨论点是口腔作为病毒传播的主要途径是否被忽视，[interludead] 和 [rickydroll] 都提到口腔健康在整体健康中的重要性，但现有手段不足。
• 对现有科学机制的有效性和特异性存在疑问，如 [hirenj] 对N-糖链结合机制的特异性表示怀疑。
• [intrasight] 提出的伐昔洛韦与痴呆症的关系是一个新颖的讨论点，扩展了抗病毒药物的潜在应用领域。

43636302.article_content:
In today’s interconnected world, infectious diseases pose an escalating threat, as demonstrated by the coronavirus pandemic and outbreaks of H1N1, SARS, Ebola, Zika, and H5N1 (bird flu) viruses—all of which have had significant global health and economic impacts.
But more common viral diseases also contribute to global health challenges and economic costs. For example, seasonal influenza epidemics occur annually, causing a substantial global disease burden and economic losses exceeding $11.2 billion each year in the United States alone. Meanwhile, herpes simplex virus-1 (HSV-1), spread primarily through oral contact, infects over two-thirds of the global population and is the leading cause of infectious blindness in Western countries.
Low vaccination rates for influenza viruses and the lack of an HSV vaccine underscore the need for a new approach—one that targets reducing viral loads at the sites where transmission occurs. And for viruses like these, which are transmitted more efficiently through the mouth than the nose, this means focusing on the oral cavity.
Now, in a study published in
Molecular Therapy
, researchers at the
School of Dental Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania
and collaborators in Finland, have done just that.
View large image
Engineering and evaluation of anti-viral bean gum.
(Image: Yuwei Guo, Rachel Kulchar, Rahul Singh, and Geetanjali Wakade/Courtesy of Henry Daniell)
Building on their
previous work
—now in
clinical trial
—showing that a similar approach was able to reduce SARS-CoV-2 in COVID-19 patient saliva or swab samples by more than 95%,
Henry Daniell
, W.D. Miller Professor in
Penn’s School of Dental Medicine
, and collaborators tested the ability of a chewing gum made from lablab beans,
Lablab purpureus
—that naturally contain an antiviral trap protein (FRIL)—to neutralize two herpes simplex viruses (HSV-1 and HSV-2) and two influenza A strains (H1N1 and H3N2). The chewing gum formulation allowed for effective and consistent release of FRIL at sites of viral infection.
They demonstrated that 40 milligrams of a two-gram bean gum tablet was adequate to reduce viral loads by more than 95%, a reduction similar to what they saw in their SARS-CoV-2 study.
Importantly, the researchers prepared the gum as a clinical-grade drug product to comply with the FDA specifications for drug products and found the gum to be safe. Daniell notes, “These observations augur well for evaluating bean gum in human clinical studies to minimize virus infection/transmission.”
Daniell and his colleagues are now looking to use lablab bean powder to tackle bird flu, which is currently having a significant impact in North America. In the previous three months,
54 million birds
have been affected by H5N1, and several human infections have been reported in the U.S. and Canada.
Previously,
bean powder was shown
by others to effectively neutralize H5N1 and H7N9—two strains of influenza A known to cause bird flu in humans as well as in birds. Daniell and colleagues are currently looking to test its use in bird feed to help control bird flu in birds.
“Controlling transmission of viruses continues to be major global challenge. A broad spectrum antiviral protein (FRIL) present in a natural food product (bean powder) to neutralize not only human flu viruses but also avian (bird) flu is a timely innovation to prevent their infection and transmission,” says Daniell.
Henry Daniell is the W.D. Miller Professor in the Department of Basic & Translational Sciences at the School of Dental Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania.
Other authors include Gary H. Cohen, Yuwei Guo, Uddhab Karki, Rachel J. Kulchar, Rahul Singh, and Geetanjali Wakade of Penn Dental Medicine, Hamid Khazaei of the Natural Resources Institute Finland (Luke) and the University of Finland and Juha-Matti Pihlava of the University of Finland.
Research performed in the Daniell lab is supported by NIH grant R01 HL 107904.

data.title: Kalshi CEO: 'State law doesn't really apply' to us
data.author: impish9208
data.article_summary: 预测市场初创公司Kalshi上周起诉新泽西和内华达州，因其试图关闭该公司最近推出的体育交易业务。Kalshi声称，作为联邦监管平台，州级博彩委员会无权为其制定规则。CEO Tarek Mansour表示，他们受联邦监管，州法律不适用。Kalshi此前曾与商品期货交易委员会（CFTC）打过重大法律战并获胜，目前正试图扩展到体育预测市场，允许用户对体育赛事下注，包括在11个赌博非法的州。然而，六个合法体育博彩的州发出停止令，认为Kalshi的体育预测市场实质上是赌博。Kalshi则认为其受CFTC许可，且其市场更像衍生品交易所而非赌博。日前，Kalshi在内华达的诉讼中首获法律胜利，获准继续运营。Kalshi与特朗普政府关系密切，曾准确预测特朗普在2024年大选中的胜选几率，并聘请特朗普之子Donald Trump Jr.为战略顾问。如果Kalshi赢得这些诉讼，可能在体育博彩市场占据重要位置，估值也将大幅提升。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[对Kalshi等类似赌博业务的看法及相关讨论]

不同观点：
• [linksnapzz] 认为，过去类似Kalshi这种"多步骤的赌博"业务可能会受到像芝加哥黑帮等非法组织的威胁，这些组织通过暴力等手段进行干预，而现在的监管机构如CFTC（商品期货交易委员会）的威慑力可能不如这些非法组织有效。该评论暗示过去的非法手段可能比现代的合法监管更具实际效果。

• [xrd] 表示之前不了解Kalshi，通过一篇博客和Michael Lewis的播客了解到相关讨论。他提到播客中讲述了Rufus Peabody通过数据驱动的方式改变了体育赌博的模式，并引用了播客中的一句有趣的话。这表明他对体育赌博的数据分析方式持积极态度，并认为这种方法在某些场景下具有创新性。

• [brutal_chaos_] 对体育赌博与选举预测的不同待遇提出疑问。他认为，既然可以通过数据预测体育结果并称之为赌博，那为什么用数据预测选举结果就不能称为赌博？他表示自己对这个话题不太了解，希望得到解释。这反映出对赌博定义和合法性问题的困惑，并试图探讨体育赌博与选举预测之间的区别。

补充讨论：
• 关于赌博合法性和定义的争议：[brutal_chaos_] 的评论引发了对体育赌博和选举预测之间区别的讨论，暗示了在不同领域使用数据预测结果可能面临不同的社会和法律标准。

• 对历史和现代监管的对比：[linksnapzz] 的评论提出了对历史非法手段和现代监管效果的比较，暗示对某些业务的监管可能不如过去的黑社会手段有效。

• 数据驱动创新的认可：[xrd] 的评论显示出对数据驱动创新的认可，特别是在体育赌博领域，这表明技术进步和数据分析正在改变传统的赌博模式。

争议焦点：赌博的定义及其在不同领域的合法性，特别是体育赌博和选举预测之间的区别。

43637444.article_content:
Last week, prediction market startup Kalshi
sued New Jersey and Nevada
after they tried to shut down its recently launched sports trading operation. In the
lawsuit
, Kalshi claimed that, since they’re a federally regulated platform, state gaming commissions don’t have the authority to set rules for them.
“We’re not necessarily very concerned [because] we are regulated at the federal level,” said Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour last week at a StrictlyVC event in San Francisco. “The state law doesn’t really apply.”
Listen on
Apple Podcasts
Listen on
Spotify
If Kalshi wins these lawsuits, the startup could secure its place in the lucrative market of sports betting. However, the legal challenge may also pave the way for a clash between state regulators and the Trump administration.
This isn’t the first time Mansour has challenged a regulator’s authority. Last year, Kalshi
won a major legal battle
against the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), allowing it to process
more than $1 billion in trades
based on the outcome of political elections in 2024.
In battling the CFTC, “we’ve had to eat a lot of s— over the last five years,” said Mansour. “I’d do it again in heartbeat.”
From political elections to sports
In January, Kalshi made the leap into prediction markets for sporting events, allowing users nationwide to bet on the outcomes of March Madness and the Super Bowl — even in the 11 states where gambling is illegal.
However, six states where sports wagering is legal — including
Nevada
,
New Jersey
,
Illinois
,
Maryland
,
Ohio
, and
Montana
— sent Kalshi cease-and-desist letters claiming its sports prediction markets are de facto sports bettings. State gaming commissions argue Kalshi is not properly licensed, nor is it paying state taxes on the sports trades it offers.
“We have a license. It’s by the CFTC,” said Mansour.
Mansour argued onstage that the real motivation behind these cease-and-desist letters was a “massive casino lobby that’s unhappy” about Kalshi’s sports trading contracts.
On Tuesday, Kalshi notched its first legal win in its lawsuit against Nevada. A federal judge ruled that Kalshi can
continue operating in the state of Nevada
, at least until the lawsuit is settled.
Prediction markets are relatively new financial instruments, meaning it’s somewhat unclear which laws apply to them and which don’t. Kalshi seems to be taking full advantage of the ambiguity, allowing users to bet on everything under the sun, from the date Elon Musk leaves DOGE to the winner of the World Series.
Nevertheless, Kalshi’s legal battle should provide some clarity on the scope of prediction markets.
Trump ties
Kalshi’s prediction market, and others like it, showed Trump would win the 2024 U.S. presidential election days ahead of election night, despite other polls suggesting otherwise. In the months since, Kalshi’s ties to the Trump administration have grown strong.
“[Kalshi] was the only source of truth that people had about the fact that Donald Trump, indeed, had a 63% chance of winning the US election,” said Mansour.
In January, Kalshi
brought on Donald Trump Jr.
, the president’s son, as a strategic adviser. In February, President Trump appointed a
former Kalshi board member to lead the CFTC
. And in March, Kalshi’s top lawyer left the company to
work with Elon Musk’s DOGE group
at the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Onstage, Mansour downplayed his reliance on the Trump administration but praised it for being “pro-innovation” in the financial services sector.
Gambling versus predicting
A key question in Kalshi’s legal battle is whether prediction markets are just plain gambling. State regulators seem to think so, but Mansour argues they’re not, he told TechCrunch onstage.
According to Mansour, gambling involves creating artificial risk and betting on it — such as rolling a die and wagering money on the number that comes up.
Instead, Kalshi’s CEO argues that prediction markets are more like derivatives exchanges, which have some risk involved but ultimately help market participants “price,” or understand the risk of, certain assets or events that would be impossible to assess otherwise. Derivatives exchanges provide unique information, so they’re granted special status.
As an example of Kalshi’s economic utility, Mansour pointed to its prediction market for the TikTok ban.
“The TikTok ban is something that you just really couldn’t price before,” said Mansour. “It’s something that’s pretty important that we didn’t have any sort of gauge on what was going to happen, so I like this market a lot.”
Of course, it benefits Mansour to make these arguments. Kalshi was last valued at $787 million, according to PitchBook data. However, if Kalshi can secure its place in the sports betting world, the startup’s valuation is likely to skyrocket even further.

Nix derivations by hand, without guessing
April 5, 2025
I went on a little low-level Nix adventure yesterday and early this morning
because of
this excellent blog post
. In it, Farid builds up the
simplest possible Nix derivation—making a file that has the contents “hello
world”. Here’s what I like about it:
No Nix language; just the really fiddly low-level bits of building a
derivation by hand
It’s incremental, building from a little friendly JSON blob and incrementally
adding scarier parts
It only uses two low-level Nix commands
One thing that I did not understand after reading, though, was where the hashes
come from. Farid’s post does the same thing that I occasionally do with the C++
or Rust compiler, where we intionally cause an error to get information that
the compiler already knows. That’s not very satisfying for someone (me) who is
starting basically from zero. So I went down a bit of a rabbit hole trying to
figure out how to manually generate these hashes.
But first, let’s get some terms out of the way. Please forgive (but help me
correct) mistakes along the way, because this is my first time messing around
with Nix.
What on earth is a derivation?
As far as I can tell, it’s a very precise recipe for building a file. It’s kind
of like a Make recipe or a shell script except all of its inputs
and outputs
refer to well-known long paths in
/nix/store
.
Here’s an example from Farid’s blog that we will be trying to replicate in this
post that has one of these path names:
{
"name"
:
"simple"
,
"system"
:
"x86_64-linux"
,
"builder"
:
"/bin/sh"
,
"outputs"
:
{
"out"
:
{
"path"
:
"/nix/store/5bkcqwq3qb6dxshcj44hr1jrf8k7qhxb-simple"
}
},
"inputSrcs"
:
[],
"inputDrvs"
:
{},
"env"
:
{
"out"
:
"/nix/store/5bkcqwq3qb6dxshcj44hr1jrf8k7qhxb-simple"
},
"args"
:
[
"-c"
,
"echo 'hello world' > $out"
]
}
In it, we have a
name
field (your pick) and a
system
field (I am guessing
there are a couple of well-known system/platform names. I am also running
x86_64 Linux by happenstance. If you follow along, your hashes will be the
same as my hashes
only if
you are on the same system, I think.).
We also have this thing called a
builder
, which is the singular command that
gets run. In this case, we also pass it
args
(at the bottom) and environment
variables from
env
. Don’t think too hard about
inputSrcs
and
inputDrvs
because they don’t come into play in this post.
Last, we have
outputs
, which, like
env
, also has this magical path name.
It’s the output file (or directory, I think) that your Nix derivation is
required to create. The name
out
in each of
outputs
and
env
is arbitrary
and I think they don’t have to have the same name. Just convention.
This derivation roughly corresponds to the following Make recipe (remember that
Make variables also start with
$
so you have to escape your shell variables
like
$${var}
):
/nix/store/5bkcqwq3qb6dxshcj44hr1jrf8k7qhxb-simple
:
export
out
=
/nix/store/5bkcqwq3qb6dxshcj44hr1jrf8k7qhxb-simple
;
\
echo
'hello world'
>
$
${out}
But where does that huge path come from?
Getting set up
I didn’t want to install Nix, so I did all of my explorations inside Docker. If
you’re not going to use Nix long-term, I recommend you do the same, since it
otherwise makes some pretty invasive system changes.
Here’s all you need to get started:
FROM
nixos/nix
AS
builder
Now you can build a Docker container:
$
docker build
.
-t
notnix
...
$
and then start
/bin/sh
, the only shell in an easy-to-remember path:
$
docker run
-i
-t
notnix /bin/sh
sh-5.2#
...
Any time I use a Nix command in the rest of the article, it’s either in a
Docker
RUN
command or in
/bin/sh
inside a running Nix container.
Now let’s find some hashes.
Finding hashes
John Ott pointed out to me that Nix
docs on store paths
had a
partial answer. He said that the path comes from hashing the ATerm
representation of the derivation with the outPath set to an empty string.
…what?
So after some digging and re-reading Farid’s post, apparently ATerm is an
old(er) configuration language that looks kind of like building OCaml variants.
And I guess it makes sense that we shouldn’t need the path to calculate the
path (otherwise we’d be in circular trouble). So I had Nix create the ATerm
form of my JSON derivation without any paths:
{
"name"
:
"simple"
,
"system"
:
"x86_64-linux"
,
"builder"
:
"/bin/sh"
,
"outputs"
:
{
"out"
:
{
}
},
"inputSrcs"
:
[],
"inputDrvs"
:
{},
"env"
:
{
},
"args"
:
[
"-c"
,
"echo 'hello world' > $out"
]
}
by running:
$
nix
--extra-experimental-features
nix-command derivation add < simple.json
/nix/store/1p6dixyqvjddfq5fmys3i55nl90ckjam-simple.drv
$
Running that command outputs the path of the ATerm form file, which we can
check out:
$
cat
/nix/store/1p6dixyqvjddfq5fmys3i55nl90ckjam-simple.drv
Derive([("out","","","")],[],[],"x86_64-linux","/bin/sh",["-c","echo 'hello world' >
$out
"],[("
out
","")])
$
You can see they are making sure to remove all whitespace, even the trailing

data.title: The Columbian Orator taught nineteenth-century Americans how to speak
data.author: samclemens
data.article_summary: 《哥伦比亚演说家》是19世纪美国广受欢迎的修辞学教科书，对弗雷德里克·道格拉斯和亚伯拉罕·林肯等历史人物产生了深远影响。12岁的道格拉斯在巴尔的摩首次接触到这本书，并用辛苦赚来的50美分购买了它。这本书不仅帮助道格拉斯学会了阅读，还激发了他对演讲的热爱，最终成为他争取自由和废奴运动的重要工具。同样，年轻的林肯在伊利诺伊州新塞勒姆时也深受此书影响，通过学习其中的经典演说和启蒙思想，提升了自己的语言能力和自我认知。该书在1797年至1860年间多次再版，成为许多美国家庭的必备书籍，反映了语言在19世纪对个人成长和公众话语的重要性。

HUMANITIES: The Magazine of the National Endowment for the Humanities
Feature
The Columbian Orator
Taught Nineteenth-Century Americans How to Speak
Among its many fans were Frederick Douglass and Abraham Lincoln
Danny Heitman
HUMANITIES, Spring 2025, Volume 46, Number 2
Photo caption
Frederick Douglass (with the title page of
The Columbian Orator
) as in the frontispiece of an 1855 edition of his autobiography.
—Wikimedia
Twitter
Facebook
One day in 1830, Frederick Douglass bought a book that changed his life. Douglass, then known as Frederick Bailey, was a twelve-year-old child enslaved in Baltimore. After hearing a group of white boys recite from
The Columbian Orator
, a grade-school textbook for teaching rhetoric, Douglass decided to get a copy for himself. Against stiff odds for slaves of the time, he learned to read, and words were his prevailing passion.
Douglass used 50 cents he’d earned working odd jobs and bought
The Columbian Orator
at a local bookshop. He fell in love with the volume and was seldom without it, carrying the book with him when he eventually escaped to freedom. With the textbook as his guide, Douglass became, in the words of biographer David W. Blight, “the greatest African American leader and orator of the nineteenth century.”
Though the legendary abolitionist read as much as he could from other sources, it’s likely that “nothing had a more immediate or lasting effect on the young Douglass’s intellectual and spiritual growth than his fortuitous discovery of
The Columbian Orator
,” Blight adds.
“Every opportunity I got, I used to read this book,” Douglass recalled. The textbook also helped shape the destiny of Douglass’s contemporary Abraham Lincoln during Lincoln’s early days in New Salem, Illinois. With little formal education, the twenty-one-year-old Lincoln “studied with relish the classical and Enlightenment-era oratory in
The Columbian Orator
during his first winter (1831–32) in New Salem on the Illinois prairie,” Blight tells readers.
In
Giants
, his 2008 book about striking parallels between Douglass and Lincoln, historian John Stauffer notes the big impact that
The Columbian Orator
had on both of their lives. Like Douglass, young Lincoln “was hungry for knowledge, and it was one of the few books he read during his formative years, along with a spelling book, the Bible, and one or two others,” Stauffer observes in recounting the role of the classic textbook in forming the future president.
For strivers like Lincoln, guides to rhetoric had a special currency in the nineteenth century. “Lincoln was born into a national culture in which language was the most widely available key to individual growth and achievement. It dominated public discourse,” scholar Fred Kaplan tells readers of his book,
Lincoln: The Biography of a Writer
. “No TVs, DVDs, computers, movie screens, radios, or electricity, and no sound bites. Language mattered because it was useful for practical communication and for learning and because it could shape and direct people’s feelings and thoughts in a culture in which spoken or written words had no rival. In Lincoln’s case it also mattered immensely because it was the tool by which he explored and defined himself.”
Douglass and Lincoln were far from alone in embracing
The Columbian Orator
, which was first published by New England educator Caleb Bingham in 1797. “The
Orator
was one of the most popular books in the new nation,” Stauffer points out. “From 1797 to 1860, it went through some 23 editions and in many American homes it was one of a handful of essential books, along with the Bible, a spelling book, and a farmer’s almanac.”
To get some idea of
The Columbian Orator’
s important role in early America, it’s perhaps best to start with its title. Although the textbook’s name might sound strange to modern ears, it would have resonated with people in Douglass and Lincoln’s time. In 1790, Congress had created the District of Columbia as the new seat of government, a nod to explorer Christopher Columbus. Even earlier, Americans had evoked a mythical heroine, Columbia, as a symbol of the emerging nation. “She was portrayed as a goddess, draped in a neoclassical gown and holding a sword, an olive branch and a laurel wreath as metaphors for justice, peace and victory,” journalist Cari Shane noted in a 2023 history of Columbia. “As Lady Columbia’s image spread across the country, particularly after the Revolution, she came to embody the nation’s highest aspirations—and its colonial ambitions. Though largely forgotten today, she reigned for two centuries as our collective emblem, and her biography offers a tale in miniature of the development of a young democracy.”
Before she was eclipsed by the Statue of Liberty as a national symbol, Columbia personified the ideals of a young republic trying to reconcile the virtues of classical antiquity with the dynamism of a country on the move.

data.author: MattSayar
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者根据产品经理（即他的妻子）的要求，为家中最重要的客户（他的孩子）开发新功能的过程。他从孩子学校作业中截取了一张不清晰的图片，利用Claude AI在短时间内制作了一款游戏，并在十分钟内完成用户验收和最终版本发布，孩子对结果很满意。尽管目前用户基数的年收入为负，但通过持续教育用户，他们期望实现快速增长。作者还提到利用ChatGPT帮助孩子学习以及开发其他数学游戏的经历。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过自定义软件和教育游戏帮助孩子学习

不同观点：
• **vunderba** 认为当前项目缺乏奖励机制，建议增加粒子效果或CSS动画等视觉激励，以增加孩子的参与度。他分享了自己十年前为帮助弟弟学习乘法表而开发教育游戏的经验。
• **jumploops** 赞赏该项目，并提到自己的妻子为他们的幼儿开发了一款简单的配对游戏，避免使用应用商店中那些花哨且易上瘾的游戏内容。
• **albert_e** 提到曾做过类似的教育项目，并建议开发一种可以根据简单需求自动生成教育应用或游戏的工具，类似于Khan Academy正在尝试的1:1辅导。
• **thomaspark** 分享了自己将孩子的拼写列表转化为类似Duolingo的体验，创建了一个定制项目以提高学习效果。
• **skeptrune** 赞赏个性化软件的发展趋势，认为这是一个值得期待的领域。
• **mushufasa** 提到在小项目中使用自定义代码工具的成功经验，但在较大的代码库中，这种方法可能导致技术实现上的问题，例如在已有系统上重复构建新认证系统。
• **keyle** 分享了自己通过快速创建生日邀请的便利，但也提到在请人开发游戏时遇到失败的经历，不过这也激发了孩子对AI错误的批判性思考。
• **bhu1st** 介绍了自己为家人孩子开发的一款字母学习游戏，虽然孩子希望增加更多功能和美观图形，但由于资源限制，项目难以进一步扩展。

补充讨论：
• **dullcrisp** 以幽默方式回应，提出是否要教孩子打曲棍球的问题，虽然与主要讨论点关系不大，但显示出对教育内容选择的不同关注。

争议焦点：
• 教育软件中的奖励机制是否必要。vunderba强调奖励机制的重要性，而jumploops则更倾向于简单而有效的学习体验，避免过度依赖视觉激励。
• 个性化软件开发的可持续性。bhu1st的项目在孩子需求增加与资源有限之间面临扩展难题，mushufasa则指出在大型项目中使用自定义代码工具可能导致技术问题。

总结：评论主要围绕通过自定义软件和教育游戏帮助孩子学习的各种尝试和观点，讨论了奖励机制、个性化软件开发的优缺点以及资源限制对项目扩展的影响。

I received a ticket from my product manager (my wife) to add a new feature for our largest customer (my kindergartner). The requirements doc included a worksheet from school that looked like this.
I took that exact screenshot (blurriness, bad lighting, scribbles, and all) and uploaded it to Claude (Sonnet 3.7), started a timer, and
asked it to make a game
.
At the eight minute mark, I performed User Acceptance Testing. Some additional UX improvements were required.
At the ten minute mark, I was able to ship the final build to production. The user was happy with the final product.
While the Annual Recurring Revenue with our current user base remains negative, we hope that executing our current strategy of consistent user education will eventually result in hockey stick growth.

data.title: Parser Combinators Beat Regexes
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在Haskell中使用正则表达式和解析器组合子解决Advent of Code问题的对比。作者首先展示了一个使用正则表达式库`pcre-heavy`处理字节字符串的解决方案，该方案能解决问题但性能较差，且存在隐含的假设（如捕获组的数量），可能导致未来运行时错误。接着，作者提供了一个基于attoparsec解析器库的解决方案，尽管代码更复杂，但更加可靠和易于维护。Haskell社区通常偏好解析器组合子而非正则表达式，因为它们更灵活且类型安全。正则表达式适用于简单情况，但在复杂或需要高性能的场景中，解析器组合子更具优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：解析器组合器与正则表达式在解析任务中的应用与选择

不同观点：
• yen223认为解析器组合器非常强大，尤其在分解复杂解析问题时，但由于来自函数式编程世界，不会成为主流。他个人认为解析器组合器让解析问题变得更加直观易懂。
• austin-cheney指出正则表达式适用于简单的搜索任务，而完整的解析器则适用于更复杂的智能解析任务。他还提到正则表达式通过嵌套可以提高搜索精度，但完整解析器的成本更高。
• kazinator讨论了正则表达式的实现问题，指出一些所谓的正则表达式并不是真正的正则表达式，而是具有额外功能的回溯器。
• arn3n表示相对于编写复杂的解析器代码，他更愿意学习使用正则表达式，认为解析器组合器的代码过于繁琐。
• pklausler分享了使用解析器组合器编写Fortran解析器的经验，强调其在处理错误恢复和复杂情况时的优势，但也指出在性能优化方面存在挑战。
• o11c提醒注意解析器组合器和正则表达式在处理不良输入时可能导致的性能问题（如指数时间复杂度）。
• kreig从理论角度指出解析器组合器能够解析的文法类型比正则表达式更多，依据是Chomsky层级理论。
• maxbond认为解析器组合器是使用文法语言和手写命令式解析器之间的良好折中，可以灵活地在文法描述和代码编写之间切换。
• virgilp比较了解析器组合器和正则表达式的实现机制和性能，认为在CPU处理速度上正则表达式的DFA有优势，但在功能上解析器组合器更强大。
• torginus认为函数式编程语言特别适合编写解析器，但解析器组合器在效率和功能上不如定制解决方案，尤其在需要添加额外特性时。
• asQuirreL认为正则表达式和解析器各有其应用场景，正则表达式适合标记化输入，而解析器适合识别结构，两者不应相互取代。
• DadBase幽默地指出在处理复杂真实数据（如CSV）时，简单的工具如awk可能更可靠。
• smcl推荐了Sprache库用于C#中的小解析任务，认为正则表达式在某些任务上显得笨重。
• henning分享了使用简单字符串搜索函数的快速实现方法，认为在某些情况下比正则表达式更高效。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于解析器组合器与正则表达式在不同场景下的优劣。一方认为解析器组合器功能强大但复杂，另一方认为正则表达式简单高效但功能有限。
• 讨论中多次提到性能问题，特别是在处理不良输入时的性能表现。
• 一些评论者分享了个人经验和具体案例，提供了实际应用中的见解和建议。

43638422.article_content:
Someone online was solving Advent of Code problems, and had a question about
last years’ day 3
. They had a working solution using regular expressions
(regexes) on
String
values, but they wanted to use
ByteString
values instead
for performance reasons. They were surprised, however, that there seems to be a
lack of community cohesion around regex libraries in Haskell.
There’s a reason for that. We generally don’t use regexes in Haskell. We use
parser combinators instead, because they are almost always better. In other
languages, it would be considered overkill to write a full parser when a simple
regex can do the same thing. In Haskell, writing a parser is no big deal. We
just do it and move on with our lives.
The regex solution
The first part of the Advent of Code problem is well suited for a regex-based
solution. Here’s what such a solution might look like in Haskell. It uses the
pcre-heavy
Haskell library which in turn calls out to the system-wide
pcre
C library for actually compiling and running the regex.
In[1]:
{-# LANGUAGE QuasiQuotes #-}
module
Main
where
import
Data.ByteString
(
ByteString
)
import
qualified
Data.ByteString.Char8
as
Char8
import
Data.Monoid
(
Sum
(
..
))
import
qualified
Text.Regex.PCRE.Heavy
as
Re
import
Text.Regex.PCRE.Heavy
(re)
test_input
::
ByteString
test_input
=
Char8.pack
"xmul(2,4)%&mul[3,7]!@^do_not_mul(5,5)+mul(32,64]then(mul(11,8)mul(8,5))"
regex_matches
::
ByteString
->
Int
regex_matches
input
=
let
--
Get a list of regex matches with numbers extracted.
--
The 're' quasi-quoter compiles the regex at compile
--
time, avoiding the runtime cost of that.
hits
=
Re.scan [re
|mul\((\d+),(\d+)\)|
] input
--
Take one hit and compute its product, converting the
--
stringified numbers into actual numbers, then wrapping
--
it up as a term in a sum.
compute (
_
, [a, b])
=
Sum
(read (Char8.unpack a)
*
read (Char8.unpack b))
in
--
Fold up all terms in the sum into a single number.
getSum (foldMap compute hits)
main
::
IO
()
main
=
do
print (regex_matches test_input)
This does the job and returns the expected sum of 161. If we run this on just
under a megabyte of input data, it takes 19 seconds on my machine, spending
almost all of that time inside the
pcre
library.
1
1
Though this is a little
strange, because if I do the same thing in Perl, it takes 0.02 seconds. I wish I
had time to investigate what goes wrong.
But the main thing I dislike about this is that there’s a very strong implicit
contract between the regex and the
compute
function. The
compute
function
assumes that there were exactly two capturing groups and that they are strings
that can safely be converted to integers. This is true, but there’s nothing in
the code making that guarantee. If those assumptions become violated a year from
now, that would not be a compiler error but an exception that interrupts the
production service at 3
am
the day before an important customer meeting.
The parser solution
For the sort of problem we are facing here, the parser-based solution does look
more complicated at first glance. Part of the reason is that the regex library
comes with a method that gets all matches, regardless of their position in the
input. Parser combinators are meant to be written to consume all of the input,
so we have to manually write the parser code that iterates the input and finds
the next match.
This solution uses the
attoparsec
library, which is made to work with
ByteString
values specifically, since the person who asked the question seemed
to care about performance.
In[2]:
module
Main
where
import
Control.Applicative
((
<|>
))
import
qualified
Data.Attoparsec.ByteString.Char8
as
Parser
import
Data.ByteString
(
ByteString
)
import
qualified
Data.ByteString.Char8
as
Char8
import
qualified
Data.Either
as
Either
test_input
::
ByteString
test_input
=
Char8.pack
"xmul(2,4)%&mul[3,7]!@^do_not_mul(5,5)+mul(32,64]then(mul(11,8)mul(8,5))"
parser_matches
::
ByteString
->
Int
parser_matches
input
=
let
--
Parse a mul instruction. Starts by reading the opening
--
sequence, then the first value, then the separator,
--
then the second value, then the terminator. Finally,
--
it returns the product of the pair of values.
mul
=
do
Parser.string (Char8.pack
"mul("
)
first
<-
Parser.decimal
Parser.char
','
second
<-
Parser.decimal
Parser.char
')'
pure (first
*
second)
--
Parse the next mul instruction. Start by trying to
--
parse a mul instruction immediately. If that fails,
--
instead (1) advance the parser one step, and
--
(2) try again.
next
=
mul
<|>
do
Parser.anyChar
next
--
Scan the entire input for all mul instructions,
--
returning the sum of their products.
scan
=
do
muls
<-
Parser.many1 next
pure (sum muls)
in
--
Run the parser over the input,
--
handling a parse error by throwing
--
an exception.
Either.fromRight (error
"Failed to parse input."
)
(Parser.parseOnly scan input)
main
::
IO
()
main
=
do
print (parser_matches test_input)

direct, monadic
style, doing just what
was requ

• smcl推荐了Sprache库用于C#中的小解析任务，认为正则表达式在某些任务上显得笨重。
• henning分享了使用简单字符串搜索函数的快速实现方法，认为在某些情况下比正则表达式更高效。

• 讨论中多次提到性能问题，特别是在处理不良输入时的性能表现。

data.title: Do charity bookshops drive out other second-hand bookshops?
data.author: fogus
data.article_summary:
文章探讨了英国旧书店数量是否减少的常见看法。作者通过统计数据表明，实际上英国的二手书店铺数量一直在增加，从1955年的523家增长到2025年的1,282家。尽管许多人主观感觉旧书店减少，尤其是因为互联网、高街租金和慈善书店的影响，但数据并不支持这种观点。

文章特别分析了慈善书店是否对传统旧书店构成威胁。尽管慈善书店数量增加，如Oxfam的店铺从2003年的60家增至2025年的约150家，但整体旧书店数量并未因此减少，仍保持在900家以上。2017年的数据显示，慈善书店和传统书店可以共存，并未出现后者被"排挤"的现象。即便在2020年至2025年间，慈善书店继续增加，但传统书店数量依然稳定。因此，文章得出结论：慈善书店并未导致传统旧书店数量的减少。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• **benoau** 认为，二手书店面临挑战，因为现在的二手商品店通过在线查询价格来销售商品，导致其价格优势不再明显，这对二手书店的生存构成威胁。
• **asciimov** 表示，其所在地区的慈善商店书籍选择不佳，多为过时的节食书籍和宗教文本。
• **detourdog** 分享了其在纽约市的经历，认为书籍收藏者希望尽可能多地接近书店，并怀念过去书店铺密集的时光。

• **xhevahir** 分享了其从慈善书店和图书馆获得书籍的经历，认为这些渠道提供了丰富的选择且价格低廉。
• **trod1234** 深入分析了二手书店和慈善书店的商业模式差异，指出慈善书店由于特殊的税收和免费库存优势，能够在市场上具有不公平的竞争优势，并可能对其他书店构成威胁。
• **DadBase** 以幽默的方式评论了书籍分类的方式。
• **stevage** 提到澳大利亚的二手书店数量减少，但没有慈善书店的影响，并对当地书店的未来表示关注。
• **cafard** 以个人经历反驳了二手书店选择不佳的观点，认为某些二手书店依然能提供很好的选择。
• **protocolture** 分享了对悉尼某书店的正面评价，认为其在竞争激烈的环境中依然表现出色。
• **shadowgovt** 对慈善书店对二手书店的影响持不在乎的态度，并将这种现象类比于图书馆或互联网对实体书店的影响。

争议焦点：
• 慈善书店与传统二手书店之间的竞争是否对后者构成威胁，以及慈善书店的商业模式是否具有不公平的优势。
• 二手书店和慈善书店在顾客眼中的价值是否相同，以及慈善书店的增长是否必然导致二手书店的衰退。

43637819.article_content:
Some years ago I started investigating the common belief
among book-collectors that there are fewer second-hand bookshops in the UK than
there used to be. As a matter of stark statistical fact, this is simply not the
case.
Of course, many people will have the subjective impression
that it is true, based on their own, partial, experience. They will know of
bookshops that have closed, and towns or cities that had several but now have
none. No-one is doubting such personal impressions.
But they are not the whole picture. The broad profile I have
established, using contemporary book trade and book-collecting directories, is
that there were 523 second-hand bookshops in the UK in 1955, about 600 in 1966,
about 750 in 1973, about 900 in 1984 and in 1995, about 950 in 1999, and 1,140
in 2014. There are 1,282 now, in April 2025. At no point does this profile show
a decrease. Even if we exclude charity bookshops, the total of all other
bookshops has been stable, at about 900+, for over forty years.
Could there have been a temporary dip in between any of
these periods? Possibly, but I have not seen any evidence of that, and it could
only have been small and of short duration given the overall upward trend.
The main reasons given for the supposed decrease are the
internet, high street rents and charity bookshops. Again, no doubt each of
these has had an impact. But bricks-and-mortar booksellers can sell via the
internet too, and booksellers can migrate to lower rent areas. Indeed, there is
some evidence of this: there are fewer city centre bookshops and more in
smaller, less expensive towns.
But what about charity bookshops? The argument here is that
these get their stock and most of their staff for free, and also enjoy tax and
business rate concessions. They therefore provide, the argument goes, unfair
competition to privately-owned bookshops. In a recent (2 April) article, ‘The
problem with Oxfam Books’, for
The Spectator
, Alexander Larman
confidently states: ‘If you’re ever wondering why many medium-sized, even
large, towns and cities in Britain don’t have second-hand bookshops any longer,
the simple answer is that the Oxfam bookshops have driven them out of business.’
In fact, over 700 places in Britain do still have a
second-hand bookshop, but, that aside, the argument sounds plausible, and I can
think of an apparent anecdotal example. York has two Oxfam Bookshops and in
recent years has lost at least six other bookshops. But in each case Oxfam was
not directly cited as the cause of closure. The reasons included retirement,
death, relocation, redevelopment, the economic climate, the pandemic.
What does the evidence show? The major introduction of
full-scale charity bookshops in the UK began around 2000.
Oxfam had opened sixty by 2003, fifteen more
were announced in 2004, and by 2009 it had 130. Other charities followed,
though on a much smaller scale.
The Book Guide
, the online listing of second-hand bookshops,
gave in August 2017 a figure for the total number of charity bookshops it
recorded: 287.
However, it also gave an overall number for all bookshops:
1,187. This means that 930 in its list were not run by charities. This would
include, as with all the other overall figures I’ve cited, not only
“traditional” bookshops but also private bookrooms open by appointment, and
antiques centres with significant book stocks, and even a few well-established
market stalls.
It will be seen that the rise of charity bookshops to
getting on for 300 had not on the face of it affected the number of other
bookshops. There were 900+ of these in the late Nineties and still 900+ in 2017
alongside the charity bookshops. The theory that charity bookshops drove out
other bookshops is not borne out by the figures in this period.
But what about the period since 2017? Well, there was not
much change in the two or three following years, certainly, since The Book
Guide showed broadly similar figures for those. But since then? From 2020 to
now?
Charity bookshops have continued to increase.
The Book Guide now lists about 150
Oxfam Bookshops, together with a further 40 of its general shops with a book
room or significant stock.
It
also lists 11 for Amnesty, 7 for the Red Cross, 6 for Age UK, and 17
named as ‘Community Bookshops’ (there are more of these, with a variety of
names). There are many others for national or local good causes.
Furthermore,
The National Trust began opening second-hand bookshops at its properties in
circa 2010 and in April 2025 reported on its website that it had “more than
240”. However, some of these are very small and so do not meet the Guide’s
criteria, and most may only be visited after paying an admission charge to the
property: The Book Guide largely omits these and so they are
additional
to its overall totals.
If the
theory that charity bookshops drive out traditional bookshops were true, we
would expect to see this major expansion lead to a clear reduction in the
latter. Has it? Have other bookshops declined
