Even in my most bullish days for OpenAI, I secretly preferred DeepMind. I felt Demis Hassabis was trustworthy in a way Sam Altman couldn't be—a true scientist, not a businessman. Also,
AlphaGo
and
AlphaZero
. To me, they're not historical milestones but nostalgia. ChatGPT is cool, but do you remember
move 37
? And the
AlphaZero-Stockfish 8 chess games
? My love and interest for AI grew parallel to DeepMind’s successes. I was rooting, almost like a sports fan, for them.
So, for years, I’ve been low-key saddened by their constant
fumbling
. They had the tech, the talent, the money, the infrastructure, the prestige, and the conviction to make ChatGPT—or whatever else they wanted—before OpenAI. They didn't. CEO Sundar Pichai was afraid to thwart Google’s main revenue source (search and ads). He chose prudence over boldness. Good—they didn’t shoot themselves in the foot.
Because they didn’t shoot
at all.
But that was the last mistake they made. Today, two and a half years after the ChatGPT debacle, Google DeepMind is winning. They are winning so hard right now that they’re screaming, “Please, please, we can’t take it anymore, it’s too much winning!” No, but really—I wonder if the only reason OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and Co. ever had the slightest chance to win is because Google fumbled that one time. They don’t anymore.
I’d been holding off on writing about Gemini 2.5. Focusing on the AI model didn’t feel like enough to tell the full story of Google’s comeback. Gemini 2.5 is only a piece—albeit a big one—of something much larger. Back in December 2024, I said they would
come out on top by the end of 2025
. We’re not even halfway there and it’s already happened. (For reasons I still don’t understand, some people genuinely thought
xAI had a shot
.)
Anyway, to avoid turning this post into an over-stylized narrative—which I do more often than I’d like—I’m keeping it to bullet points. It hits harder that way. You’ll see what I mean when the list just... doesn’t end.
Google and DeepMind fans: enjoy the long-overdue rebirth.
Gemini 2.5 Pro Experimental
is the best model in the world. Number one on the
LMArena
,
GPQA Diamond
,
Humanity's Last Exam
, and AIME (math competition). It's also the best on private benchmarks like
Aider Polyglot
(code),
Live Bench
(diverse). It's better than Claude Sonnet at
playing Pokemon
(a promising agentic playground) and rising quickly on
Minecraft Bench
(some
examples
). It is decent at
creative writing
(e.g.,
long-context comprehension
), which has been an elusive milestone for years.
Source
Perhaps most importantly, the benchmark scores match the signal I receive from vibes checks, high-taste testers, and firsthand testimonials:
people
are
reporting
en masse
that
Gemini
2.5
Pro
is
indeed
the
best
model
today
. A rare sight to witness. (Watch
Matthew Berman’s clip
below.)
And that's just pure performance. Add to the above that Gemini 2.5, compared to models of its category, is
fast
and
cheap
—I mean, they're
giving away free access
!—has a gigantic
context window of 1 million tokens
(only recently surpassed by Meta’s Llama 4) and it’s connected to the entire Google suite of products (more on that soon).
Source
Gemini 2.5 Flash (
launching soon
) is Gemini 2.5 Pro’s little brother. It is just as amazing but for a different reason. Together with old versions of Flash (
2.0
,
Lite
,
Thinking
), it will be
extremely fast
and
extremely cheap
(much cheaper than comparable models from competitors,
even DeepSeek’s
, famous for
being cheap
). They're also small, which makes them perfect for edge applications and phone integration.
Source
Then there’s
Gemma 3
—Google’s open source model,
competitive with the best open-source models
, including Llama 4 (
too big
) and DeepSeek-V3.
Swyx plotted a graph
revealing that “Google owns the Pareto frontier” with Gemini 2.0/2.5 (both Pro and Flash) on the two most important metrics: performance and cost. Not only that, but Google's most performant models
remain cost-effective,
and its most cost-effective models
remain performant
. Google is bullying the competition at this point; Gemini is off the charts, literally.
Source
The LLMs that underlie chatbots like Gemini and ChatGPT are the main attraction but far from the only one. Google dominates the other generative AI areas just as clearly as it dominates text-based models. They announced they will integrate the other AI tools they have into
Vertex AI
:
Lyria
(music),
Imagen 3
(image),
Veo 2
(video), and
Chirp 3
(voice/speech). These are, in a way, side-projects for Google. Still, they’re world-class in their respective categories. Arguably,

data.title: America Is Backsliding Toward Its Most Polluted Era
data.author: pmags
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了美国空气污染的严重健康危害及其背后的政治因素。尽管空气质量有所改善，但微小颗粒物仍能深入人体，引发哮喘、心脏病、抑郁、甚至痴呆等多种疾病，尤其对儿童影响更大。文章指出，美国每年因颗粒物污染导致的死亡人数远超交通事故。尽管拜登政府曾计划加强 particulate matter 的标准，但特朗普政府却通过政策回滚和削减环保规则，可能导致污染加剧。 EPA 计划撤销多项环境规定，包括放宽颗粒物标准，这将对公共健康构成威胁。尽管美国的空气比过去清洁，但仍有三分之一的美国人生活在空气有害的地区，而政府政策的改变可能使空气质量进一步恶化。

When you inhale a microscopic speck of soot, its journey may go like this: The particle enters your nose and heads into your lungs, penetrating even the tiny air sacs that facilitate gas exchange. Next it may slip into your bloodstream and flow into your heart, or past the blood-brain barrier. Most of us inhale some of these tiny particles every day. But inhaling enough can turn the act of breathing into an existential hazard, prompting or worsening asthma, COPD, respiratory infections, and permanent lung damage. In the heart, the specks can trigger heart disease, heart attacks, and most of the cardiovascular disorders you can think of. Air pollution is also associated with
depression and
anxiety
, and with higher
rates
of suicide. It can trigger strokes and is linked to
dementia
or—even at average levels in this country—
Parkinson’s disease
.
These particles
can also cross the placenta
, where they can reduce an infant’s
lung function
before birth. A pre-polluted baby is also more likely to arrive
prematurely
, and at a
lower weight
. Exposure to bad air in utero is associated with a
higher risk of autism
, and exposure in childhood has been linked to
behavioral
and
cognitive
problems, including lower IQ. A person’s lungs can develop until age 25, and as Alison Lee, a pulmonologist at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, put it to me, “once you’ve lost lung function, you can’t get it back.” Persistent exposure to air pollution can cause permanent harm, creating health problems for children and setting them up to become sicker adults.
It’s hard to picture a person dropping dead from air pollution, yet it happens all the time. In the United States, particulate matter is estimated to kill more than twice as many people as vehicular accidents do—in total,
some 100,000
to
200,000
people a year, as an underlying factor of chronic disease or by way of heart attacks, asthma attacks, and other sudden events. Even as air quality in America has improved, researchers have found that relatively low concentrations of particulate matter can cause major hazards.
All of this stems from a toxic and mostly invisible danger, largely the product of
burning things
for fuel and letting the remnant drift into the air and then into us—which is what happens unless the government regulates that process. The Trump administration, however, has shown little interest in doing so. Through new policies and aggressive cuts, the administration is taking steps that will encourage more pollution while muffling the science that shows the harms. The very air that Americans breathe will likely become less safe.
So far, the EPA has announced that it will pursue
a suite of rollbacks
of environmental rules, among them a Joe Biden–era update to standards
for particulate matter
that were meant to be fully in force by 2032 and that the Biden EPA
projected
would, in that year alone, prevent up to 4,500 premature deaths and 800,000 cases of asthma, reaping up to $46 billion in health benefits. It also plans to reassess a rule limiting the amount of airborne mercury and arsenic that power plants can release. In a statement
announcing

data.title: Are .NET 4.x and JDK 8.x the "zombie" runtimes of enterprise software?
data.author: pyeri
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：.NET和Java技术栈的版本迁移和遗留系统维护问题

不同观点：
• **haroldfredshort**: 认为Windows 11仍然包含非常古老的Visual Basic 6运行时，说明许多系统依赖这些旧技术。微软对遗留系统的支持较长时间存在。
   
• **eterm**: 指出从.NET Framework迁移到.NET Core/.NET 6+并不像微软宣传的那样顺利。尤其是.NET 6的支持周期短，企业更偏向使用生命周期更长的.NET 4.8。奇数版本的.NET不被企业考虑。

• **y42**: 描述了一个基于.NET 4.6.x的ETL系统，由于紧密绑定在微软生态上（如Windows Server和SSIS），系统难以维护，且团队拒绝改变，导致技术债务累积。这种“从不改变运行中的系统”的态度可能导致未来更大的问题。

• **fhd2**: 提到一些初创公司因为早期使用ASP.NET构建MVP而陷入.NET Framework的遗留问题，导致后续性能和开发效率问题，迁移到.NET Core和PostgreSQL需要大量投资，很多公司难以承担。

• **jmull**: 认为微软没有为.NET Framework提供兼容的迁移路径，导致许多公司只能继续使用.NET Framework直到无法运行。即使微软不再支持，遗留系统也会通过其他方式维持运行。

• **joseda-hg**: 认为.NET Framework还会存在几十年，特别是微软自己的一些产品（如Office和Sharepoint）仍依赖它。对.NET Standard 2.0的支持使得部分现代化是可行的。

• **smileybarry**: 分享了在企业产品中从.NET 4.x迁移到新版.NET时遇到的实际问题，包括对旧操作系统的支持、安装包大小以及技术决策上的保守态度。

• **alkonaut**: 指出.NET 4.X作为Windows组件会长期存在，尤其在桌面应用中，因为不需要额外部署运行时，迁移到新版.NET的收益不明显。

• **ivolimmen**: 提到Java 8到Java 9的迁移因为模块化和外部依赖问题变得复杂，导致许多企业延迟升级。

• **stevoski**: 认为Java的版本更新总体上是平滑的，除了Java 8到Java 9的升级。企业IT部门因预算和人力资源问题，通常不会优先进行此类升级。

补充讨论：
• **naasking**: 提出行业惯性是合理的，团队在没有商业需求的情况下不愿重写系统。
• **PaulHoule**: 提到JDK 8后的反射机制变化导致一些代码需要调整。
• **dachris**: 分享了从ASP.NET Framework迁移到ASP.NET Core的实际经验，指出虽然总体顺利但仍需处理许多细节问题，整个过程耗时数周。

争议焦点：
• 微软对.NET Framework的支持和企业对遗留系统的依赖之间的矛盾。
• 从.NET Framework迁移到.NET Core/.NET 6+的实际困难和成本问题。
• Java 8到Java 9升级的复杂性以及企业为何迟迟不升级。

总结：
评论中主要讨论了.NET和Java技术栈中的遗留系统迁移问题，强调了企业由于技术债务、成本和惯性而不愿升级到新版本，同时指出了在实际迁移过程中遇到的困难和挑战。

data.title: Controlling Language and Diffusion Models by Transporting Activations
data.author: 2bit
data.article_summary: 苹果公司研究人员开发了一种名为Activation Transport（AcT）的新技术，用于精细控制生成模型的输出。与依赖强化学习与人类反馈（RLHF）或指令微调的传统方法不同，AcT不改变模型参数，而是在推理时动态调整输出，避免了计算开销和性能影响。该方法利用最优传输理论，在源激活和目标激活分布之间建立映射，确保调整后的激活仍在模型训练期间学习的分布范围内，从而减少意外行为和性能下降。AcT提供了更可靠的结果，且无需大量数据和复杂计算，相比提示工程更具优势。该研究将在ICLR 2025上作为 spotlight 展示，代码已开放。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于多模态LLM（大型语言模型）的控制与优化方案的讨论，尤其是如何有效移除或控制特定概念（如“粉色大象”），以及相关技术（如LoRA、Optimal Transport Map）的实现和应用。

不同观点：
• [scorps] 认为人类在处理“不要想粉色大象”这样的问题上存在共性，暗示控制某些特定概念的难度。
• [sampton] 提出多模态LLM是真正的解决方案，但苹果公司可能在寻找能在当前设备上运行的方案，强调设备本地运行的需求。
• [vessenes] 详细解释了一种通过“Optimal Transport Map”来移除特定概念的方法，并讨论了该方法的实现细节和潜在问题，比如是否类似于低秩适配器（LoRA）或平均差异的计算。
• [roro_7] 认为模型越智能越难控制，提出如果完全控制模型，可能会导致模型变得不智能，强调独立思考是智能模型的核心特性。
• [bradneuberg] 认为这项技术是一个重要的突破，提供了一种非RHLF（基于人类反馈的强化学习）机制来限制和聚焦深度网络。
• [imranq] 认为这实际上只是用一种复杂的方式描述LoRA，本质上仍是基于特定输出学习权重并应用于推理。
• [turnsout] 对苹果公司严格控制输出的兴趣表示理解，并猜测这项工作是否已经应用于Image Playground。
• [antonkar] 提出了一种与AI安全相关的创业想法，涉及将消费级GPU整合到云中以提高安全性，并分享利润，但该评论与主要讨论点关系较远。

补充讨论：
• 关于“Optimal Transport Map”的具体实现存在争议，[vessenes] 和 [imranq] 都提到了它是否与LoRA或简单的权重调整类似，但未达成一致。
• [roro_7] 强调了模型智能与控制之间的权衡，暗示完全控制可能导致模型失去独立性和智能性，这是一个值得注意的讨论点。
• 不同评论者对技术实现细节的关注点各异，有的关注实际应用（如[sampton]和[turnsout]），有的则关注理论和机制（如[vessenes]和[imranq]）。

Controlling Language and Diffusion Models by Transporting Activations
Large generative models are becoming increasingly capable and more widely deployed to power production applications, but getting these models to produce exactly what's desired can still be challenging. Fine-grained control over these models' outputs is important to meet user expectations and to mitigate potential misuses, ensuring the models' reliability and safety. To address these issues, Apple machine learning researchers have developed a new technique that is modality-agnostic and provides fine-grained control over the model's behavior with negligible computational overhead, while minimally impacting the model's abilities.
Activation Transport (AcT)
is a general framework to steer activations guided by optimal transport theory that generalizes many previous activation-steering works. The work will be presented as a Spotlight at
ICLR 2025
, and code is available
here
.
To help generative models produce output that aligns with their users' expectations, researchers often rely on reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) or instruction fine-tuning, but these approaches are resource-intensive and become increasingly impractical as models grow in complexity. In addition, changing a model's parameters can have unintended consequences, affecting its overall performance on other tasks.
To control the output of these generative models, users often try crafting precise prompts, but while this is more accessible, it offers limited controls. Even with carefully constructed prompts, a modelâs output can be unpredictable and lacking the nuance a user might need. For example, itâs common for models to fail when prompted with instructions not to include something
(see figure 1)
:
Figure 1: Text-to-Image model such as SDXL and FLUX.1.dev tend to generate pink elephants even when instructed not to generate one. Left: âAn astronaut in a space station. Do not show a pink elephantâ. Right: âA dog running on the beach splashing water. Do not show a pink elephantâ.
In many applications, such as content generation, creative writing, or even AI-assisted design, having fine-grained control over the model's output is crucial. For example, a user might want to adjust the tone of text without altering its content, change the style of generated images while maintaining their context, or to ensure sensitive topics are handled with care, without compromising overall coherence. Activation Transport (AcT) delivers this, without the computational overhead, complexity, and volume of data required by RLHF or fine-tuning, and with more reliable results than prompt engineering.
Activation Steering: A simple-yet-powerful solution
The computational and economic cost of fine-tuning large models as well as the need for fine-grained control has motivated research on targeted interventions upon model activations to modify specific behaviors in a fine-grained way. The main advantage of these "activation steering" methods is that they do not require back-propagation and typically can be merged into the model weights.
Unlike RLHF or fine-tuning, activation steering doesn't impact a model's parameters, but instead leverages an understanding of the model's operations to dynamically steer its outputs in a desired direction at inference time.
Prior approaches to activation steering have used a vector-based intervention that take the source activations of expert neurons, and shift them toward a learned target
(see figure 2)
. However, the degree to which activations are shifted is controlled by an unbounded model-level parameter (Î»\lambda), making interpretable interventions challenging. Additionally, these interventions can shift activations out of distribution, meaning that the shifted activations can end up far from what the model has learned to expect during training, resulting in a disruption of the model's natural dynamics, which can lead to unexpected behavior and reduced performance.
Figure 2: Prior Activation Steering works using vector-based steering will likely move activations out of distribution. The intervention strength parameter Î» is unbounded and non-interpretable.
Activation Transport (AcT) and Linear-AcT
Activation Transport (AcT) is a novel intervention framework that surpasses the prior limitations of activation steering by accounting for distributions of source and target activations, and using an interpretable and actionable strength parameter for fine-grained control.
AcT learns the Optimal Transport (OT) map between the source and target activation distributions. This ensures that an activation transported from the source will comply with the target distribution, minimizing the compounding effects on the dynamics of the model itself. • 不同评论者对技术实现细节的关注点各异，有的关注实际应用（如[sampton]和[turnsout]），有的则关注理论和机制（如[vessenes]和[imranq]）。

主要讨论点：R语言及其相关工具（如dplyr/tidyverse）在数据处理和分析中的应用，以及与Python的比较和整合问题。

不同观点：
• **支持R语言的观点**：[cye131] 认为R，尤其是dplyr/tidyverse，被低估了。相比Python的pandas等工具，R在数据分析和调试方面更加高效和直观，能减少复杂性并加快基本分析的速度。
• **对R和Python的混合看法**：[uptownfunk] 认为虽然R在数据处理和分析方面具有优雅和直观的优势，但Python在工程效率上更胜一筹，尤其是在使用LLM（大语言模型）的情况下，因此更倾向于使用Python。
• **R的工程问题**：[uptownfunk] 提到R在命名空间和导入系统上存在问题，导致在工程应用中不如Python高效。

补充讨论：
• **R的文档功能**：[thangalin] 提到R可以帮助生成动态Markdown文档（.Rmd文件），并介绍了相关工具（如knitr和KeenWrite），展示了R在文档处理方面的应用。
• **R的资源推荐**：[vharuck] 分享了一个针对R新手的指南，其中包含常见的陷阱和建议，为新手提供学习资源。
• **R与Python的整合问题**：[kingkongjaffa] 提问如何将R代码与Python后端有效整合，反映出实际应用中跨语言整合的需求。
• **其他资源和工具的提及**：[LostMyLogin] 提醒不要将不同的R书籍混淆，[madcaptenor] 建议在资源列表中区分免费和付费书籍，[hughess] 分享了自己在金融领域使用R的经验，并提到R对当前项目的启发。
• **R对LLM的支持问题**：[brcmthrowaway] 直接提问R是否支持LLM，表明对R在大语言模型应用中的能力存在疑问。

争议焦点：R和Python在数据处理和工程应用中的优劣比较，特别是在命名空间管理、工程效率和LLM支持方面的差异。

43646219.article_content:
1
Your last-ever bookmark
Thanks for stopping by. If you’re like me, you can’t help but bookmark every R-related programming book you find in the hopes that one day you, or someone you know, might find it useful.
Hopefully this is the only bookmark you’ll need in future ;).
When I initially released this collection in late August 2020, it contained about 100 books that I’d been collecting over the previous two years. Since then I’ve found a few more and there have been contributions from many people. The collection now stands at over 400 free, open-sourced books.
Most of these are free. Some are paid but usually quite affordable.
1.1
Searching
If there’s something specific you’re looking for, use the menu or search using the magnifying glass icon at the top of the screen.
1.2
Supporting
If you’d like to show your appreciation with a donation you’re most welcome to do so here:
1.3
Contributing
Please feel free to contribute paid and free books - see
GitHub.
or submit via the
Google Form
.
1.4
Big thanks to Fathom Data
I want to give a special thanks to the folks at
Fathom Data
who converted the site from bookdown to Quarto. I’ve worked with Fathom Data for many years and can highly recommend their services!
1.5
License
This website/book is free to use, and is licensed under the
Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs 3.0 License
.
1.6
Live stats
Who says you can’t have privacy AND transparency??
I’m guessing that if you’re interested in R then you also like data ;).
Note that “unique” visits will be higher in Plausible than you’d find with Google Analytics. Because Plausible is GDPR compliant and privacy focused, each user is identified for only 1 day. If someone visits the site 2 days in a row, that’s counted as 2 “uniques” whereas in Google Analytics it would only be counted as 1 unique visitor because of the presence of persistent cookies and such that allows for tracking of users.
From now on, you can view the
LIVE site stats right here
.
1.7
About me
I’m Oscar. If you like this book, feel free to say “Hi!” on
Mastodon
or
LinkedIn
.
If you want to stay in the loop on other data-related products I create, or major updates to this book, sign up to my
newsletter
.

data.title: Usability Improvements in GCC 15
data.author: dmalcolm
data.article_summary:
文章总结了GCC 15编译器在可用性方面的六项改进，重点介绍了诊断信息的美观性和易读性提升。主要内容包括：

1. **更美观的执行路径**：通过添加警告表情符号（⚠️）和ASCII艺术展示控制流，帮助用户更直观地理解代码问题。
2. **C++模板错误的新外观**：简化和重构C++模板错误信息，使其更易读。例如，将原先GCC 14中长达34行的错误信息进行优化，使其更简洁。

其他改进还包括对诊断信息中Unicode字符的使用、减少视觉噪音等，旨在提升开发者的使用体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GCC编译器的改进、错误信息显示以及与其他编译器（如Clang）的比较

不同观点：
• [mwkaufma] 对文章的可用性提出改进请求，特别提到不要劫持浏览器的后退按钮，这可能与用户体验相关。
• [munificent] 认为通过层次结构显示模板错误是非常明智的做法，并解释了这种方法在处理C++模板和SFINAE属性时的重要性，支持GCC的这一改进。
• [porphyra] 赞同GCC错误信息嵌套显示的方式，认为这样更容易阅读，只需关注最高缩进级别。
• [jmclnx] 讨论了GCC因GPL可能在Linux中保持默认编译器的地位，但预计Clang有一天会成为默认编译器，同时提到COBOL被合并到GCC中的消息。
• [codeshaunted] 支持GCC的改进，但不喜欢控制台中出现的表情符号。
• [levodelellis] 希望GCC提供一个配置文件或环境变量，以允许用户自定义单行错误信息，并希望能够扩展错误信息，增加自定义消息的功能。
• [jart] 提供了GCC 15发布 notes 的链接，并对其中一些优化和新特性提出了具体的技术问题和建议，例如对__builtin_stdc_rotate_left()的必要性提出质疑。
• [Night_Thastus] 支持更好的错误信息显示，期待GCC的改进能在Windows开发环境中应用。
• [meisel] 认为模板错误信息显示的改进很好，并建议为Clang和旧版GCC用户编写错误信息翻译工具。
• [kazinator] 对现代编译器诊断的复杂性提出批评，认为简单的GCC 3.4.6已经非常易用，质疑现代化的必要性。
• [wiseowise] 对现代错误信息中使用表情符号的做法表示不满，幽默地提到下一步可能会有“错误的表情符号”。
• [brcmthrowaway] 询问GCC插件的现状。
• [budmichstelk] 支持GCC的现代化努力，认为很多旧问题已经解决，并且有很多新的改进。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是编译器错误信息显示的复杂性和现代化是否有必要，部分用户如[kazinator]更喜欢简单的错误信息，而其他用户如[porphyra]和[Night_Thastus]则欢迎改进。
• 技术细节如[jart]提到的优化和内建函数的必要性也是讨论的一个重要方面。
• 用户对表情符号在错误信息中的使用存在分歧，部分用户如[codeshaunted]和[wiseowise]表示不喜欢。
• 对GCC插件的现状也引起了一些用户的关注。

43643886.article_content:
6 usability improvements in GCC 15
April 10, 2025
David Malcolm
Related topics:
C
C++
Compilers
Linux
Secure Coding
Related products:
Red Hat Enterprise Linux
Share:
Table of contents:
I work at Red Hat on
GCC, the GNU Compiler Collection
. I spent most of the past year working on how GCC emits diagnostics (errors and warnings) in the hope of making it easier to use. Let's take a look at 6 improvements to look forward to in the upcoming GCC 15.
1. Prettier execution paths
I added a
static analyzer to GCC in GCC 10
that prints visualizations of predicted paths of execution through the user's code, demonstrating each problem it predicts.
Here's an example that shows some of the improvements I've made to this in GCC 15:
infinite-loop-linked-list.c: In function ‘while_loop_missing_next’:
infinite-loop-linked-list.c:30:10: warning: infinite loop [CWE-835] [-Wanalyzer-infinite-loop]
30 |   while (n)
|          ^
‘while_loop_missing_next’: events 1-3
30 |   while (n)
|          ^
|          |
|          (1) ⚠️  infinite loop here
|          (2) when ‘n’ is non-NULL: always following ‘true’ branch... ─>─┐
|                                                                         │
|                                                                         │
|┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
31 |│    {
32 |│      sum += n->val;
|│             ~~~~~~
|│              |
|└─────────────>(3) ...to here
‘while_loop_missing_next’: event 4
32 |       sum += n->val;
|       ~~~~^~~~~~~~~
|           |
|           (4) looping back... ─>─┐
|                                  │
‘while_loop_missing_next’: event 5
|                                  │
|┌─────────────────────────────────┘
30 |│  while (n)
|│         ^
|│         |
|└────────>(5) ...to here
I've added a warning emoji (⚠️) to the event in the path where the problem occurs (event 1 in the above), and I've added "ASCII art" to show control flow, such as the lines connecting events 2 and 3, and those connecting events 4 and 5 (compare with the
GCC 14 output seen here
).
Another example of an execution path can be seen in this new
-fanalyzer
warning
-Wanalyzer-undefined-behavior-ptrdiff
, which warns about pointer subtractions involving different chunks of memory:
demo.c: In function ‘test_invalid_calc_of_array_size’:
demo.c:9:20: warning: undefined behavior when subtracting pointers [CWE-469] [-Wanalyzer-undefined-behavior-ptrdiff]
9 |   return &sentinel - arr;
|                    ^
events 1-2
│
│    3 | int arr[42];
│      |     ~~~
│      |     |
│      |     (2) underlying object for right-hand side of subtraction created here
│    4 | int sentinel;
│      |     ^~~~~~~~
│      |     |
│      |     (1) underlying object for left-hand side of subtraction created here
│
└──> ‘test_invalid_calc_of_array_size’: event 3
│
│    9 |   return &sentinel - arr;
│      |                    ^
│      |                    |
│      |                    (3) ⚠️  subtraction of pointers has undefined behavior if they do not point into the same array object
│
There's a line on the left-hand side that visualizes the stack depth to highlight calls and returns.  As of GCC 15 this now uses unicode box-drawing characters (where the locale supports this), and for purely intraprocedual cases like the
-Wanalyzer-infinite-loop
example above, we now omit it altogether, which saves some visual "noise."
2. A new look for C++ template errors
Compiler errors involving C++ templates are notoriously difficult to read.
Consider this invalid C++ code:
struct widget {};
void draw (widget &);
struct diagram {};
void draw (diagram &);
template <class W>
concept drawable = requires(W w) { w.draw (); };
template <drawable T>
void draw(T);
int main ()
{
draw (widget ());
}
Attempting to
compile it with GCC 14
with
-fconcepts -fconcepts-diagnostics-depth=2
gives 34 lines of output, which is relatively simple as far as these go, and even this can be hard to decipher. I'll post it here for reference, but I confess that my eyes tend to glaze over when I try to read it:
<source>: In function 'int main()':
<source>:15:8: error: no matching function for call to 'draw(widget)'
15 |   draw (widget ());
|   ~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~~
<source>:2:6: note: candidate: 'void draw(widget&)' (near match)
2 | void draw (widget &);
|      ^~~~
<source>:2:6: note:   conversion of argument 1 would be ill-formed:
<source>:15:9: error: cannot bind non-const lvalue reference of type 'widget&' to an rvalue of type 'widget'
15 |   draw (widget ());
|         ^~~~~~~~~
<source>:5:6: note: candidate: 'void draw(diagram&)'
5 | void draw (diagram &);
|      ^~~~
<source>:5:12: note:   no known conversion for argument 1 from 'widget' to 'diagram&'
5 | void draw (diagram &);
|            ^~~~~~~~~
<source>:11:6: note: candidate: 'template<class T>  requires  drawable<T> void draw(T)'
11 | void draw(T);
|      ^~~~
<source>:11:6: note:   template argument deduction/substitution failed:
<source>:11:6: note: constr

data.title: Garfield Minus Garfield
data.author: mike1o1
data.article_summary: "Garfield Minus Garfield"是一个网站，专门将《加菲猫》漫画中的加菲猫角色移除，以展现主角乔恩·阿布库的内心困境。这使得漫画变成了一种对孤独和抑郁的深刻探索，反映了乔恩在一个安静的美国郊区的孤独生活。网站由丹·沃尔什创建，通过社交媒体和RSS提供更新，并托管在Tumblr上。该项目还提供了档案和常见问题解答，并公开了原作者的看法和网站的Twitter动态。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“Garfield Minus Garfield”项目的各种观点和讨论

不同观点：
• [nickvec] 认为“Garfield Minus Garfield”揭示了Jon Arbuckle的孤独与抑郁，使读者在某种程度上产生共鸣。这个评论强调了对Jon存在主义焦虑的解读。
• [grepLeigh] 提到了该项目的多年前互联网背景（通过Stumbleupon发现），并对该项目至今仍然存在表示欣喜。
• [jf] 指出该项目得到了原作者Jim Davis的认可，并且还出版了官方书籍，强调了该项目在主流文化中的合法性。

data.title: A surprising enum size optimization in the Rust compiler
data.author: returningfory2
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了Rust编译器对枚举类型内存表示的优化。枚举类型由多个变体组成，每个变体可以有不同的数据 payload。通常，枚举的大小是最大变体的大小加上用于标识变体的标签（tag）的大小。文章详细解释了如何通过打印内存表示来观察这些标签和数据。

文章还介绍了“niche 优化”，这是一种针对只有一个变体带有 payload 的枚举的优化。例如，`Option<char>` 枚举通过利用无效的 char 值来表示 `None`，从而无需额外的标签字节。

文章最后提到了一种新的优化发现，涉及嵌套枚举。例如，嵌套的 `Inner` 枚举按预期占用 8 字节，但通过进一步优化，Rust 编译器能够更有效地表示这些嵌套结构。这种优化超出了已知的 niche 优化，展示了 Rust 编译器在处理复杂枚举时的智能优化策略。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust中无效UTF-8字符引发的未定义行为及niche优化的相关技术

不同观点：
• [mmastrac] 认为Rust中的`char`类型作为一种特殊的整数类型，拥有有效范围的子范围。如果从一个无效字符串构造出无效的`char`，可能会绕过niche优化，导致不安全的transmute，破坏程序的健全性（soundness）。
• [pitaj] 反驳mmastrac对niche优化的理解有限，指出外层枚举通过使用内层枚举的标签空间来优化其判别式（discriminant），这实际上就是niche优化。
• [Joker_vD] 补充说明了在ML等语言中也有类似的压缩枚举的技巧，但这些技巧的回报随着复杂性增加而迅速减少，而且这些技巧通常只适用于模块内的数据类型，类似于Rust中的抽象数据类型。
• [packetlost] 则从内存对齐和字节填充的角度解释了问题，认为这可能并不是简单的枚举扁平化，而是32位对齐要求和子字节判别式大小导致的结果。他还提到嵌套的match语句可以被扁平化为跳转列表。

补充讨论：
• [kazinator] 认为这种技术可以总结为标签合并（tag merging），当一个枚举的成员是另一个枚举时，两个枚举可以合并成一个判别式标签，而不是分别测试，这样可以有效地减少空间占用。
• [subarctic] 关心这种优化技术的实现时间，回忆以前需要手动优化嵌套枚举以节省空间。
• [lordnacho] 提出两个问题：niche优化是否需要编译器对类型有特定了解，以及如何实现一个更高级的内存布局可视化工具，特别是能识别指针的工具。

争议焦点：
• 对niche优化的理解和定义存在分歧。mmastrac认为无效字符会绕过niche优化，而pitaj则认为mmastrac对niche优化的理解有误。
• 对内存布局和优化的技术细节有不同解释，packetlost从对齐和填充角度解释，而kazinator则从标签合并角度说明。

A surprising enum size optimization in the Rust compiler
April 7, 2025
Enums are one of the most popular features in Rust.
An enum is type whose value is one of a specified set of variants.
/// Foo is either a 32-bit integer or character.
enum Foo {
Int(u32),
Char(char),
}
Values of type
Foo
are either
integers (e.g. the variant
Foo::Int(3)
with a payload of
3
)
or characters (e.g. the variant
Foo::Char('A')
with a payload of
'A'
).
If you think of structs as being the
and
combination of their fields,
enums are the
or
combination of their variants.
This post is about a surprising optimization that the Rust compiler
performs on the memory representation of enum values
in order to make their memory usage smaller
(spoiler: it’s not the niche optimization).
In general, keeping values small can result in faster programs because values get passed
around in CPU registers and more values fit in single CPU cache lines.
Generally the size of an enum is the size of the largest payload,
plus some extra bytes for storing a
tag
that specifies which variant the value is.
For the type
Foo
above, both variant payloads take up 4 bytes,
and we need an additional byte at least for the tag.
A requirement called “type alignment” (which I won’t get into)
requires that Rust actually use 4 bytes for the tag.
So the overall size of the type is 8 bytes:
assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<Foo>(), 8);
(All the code snippets can be run
here in the Rust Playground
.)
For the rest of this article it will be useful and interesting to actually see the memory
representation of various enum values.
Here’s a function that prints the raw bytes representation of any Rust value:
/// Print the memory representation of a value of a type T.
fn print_memory_representation<T: std::fmt::Debug>(t: T) {
print!("type={} value={t:?}: ", std::any::type_name::<T>());
let start = &t as *const _ as *const u8;
for i in 0..std::mem::size_of::<T>() {
print!("{:02x} ", unsafe {*start.offset(i as isize)});
}
println!();
}
(This function was adapted from this
10-year old Reddit post
.)
Let’s run this for our enum
Foo
.
print_memory_representation(Foo::Int(5));
// type=Foo value=Int(5): 00 00 00 00 05 00 00 00
//                        |-- tag --| |- value -|
print_memory_representation(Foo::Char('A'));
// type=Foo value=Char('A'): 01 00 00 00 41 00 00 00
//                           |-- tag --| |- value -|
The first thing to point out is that this computer’s memory is
little endian
,
so the lowest bytes come first.
In 32-bit hex the number 5 is
0x00000005
, but its little endian representation is
05 00 00 00
.
With that in mind, we see that the first 4 bytes are the tag.
The integer variant has been assigned tag 0,
and the character variant tag 1.
The second 4 bytes are then just the usual values of the payload.
Note that the lowercase letter “a” is 41 in ASCII,
which is why its memory representation is
41 00 00 00
.
The niche optimization
Aside from the general tags scheme,
there is one well known enum size optimization called the niche optimization.
This optimization works for types where only one of the variants has a payload.
A good example is the built in option type:
enum Option<char> {
None,
Some(char),
}
Based on the tags analysis in the last section we might guess the enum size will be 8 bytes
(the largest payload of 4 bytes plus 4 bytes for the tag).
But actually values of this type only use 4 bytes of memory in total:
assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<Option<char>>(), 4);
What’s going on?
The Rust compiler knows that while
char
takes up 4 bytes of memory,
not every value of those 4 bytes is a valid value of
char
.
Char only has about
2^21
valid values (one for each Unicode code point),
whereas 4 bytes support
2^32
different values.
The compiler choses one of these invalid bit patterns as a
niche
.
It then represents the enum value without using tags.
It represents the
Some
variant identically to char.
It represents the
None
variant using the niche.
One interesting question is: what exact niche does Rust use?
Let’s print the memory representations to see:
let a: char = 'A'
print_memory_representation(a);
// type=char value='A': 41 00 00 00
print_memory_representation(Some(a));
// type=Option<char> value=Some('A'): 41 00 00 00
let none: Option<char> = None;
print_memory_representation(none);
// type=Option<char> value=None: 00 00 11 00
As we see, the memory representations of
'A'
and
Some('A')
are identical.
Rust represents
None
using the 32-bit number
0x00110000
.
A quick search reveals that this number is exactly one bigger than the largest
valid Unicode code point.
Beyond the niche optimization?
My understanding was that Rust doesn’t perform any more optimizations,
so I was pleasantly surprised recently when I found one.
The context is nested enums. Start with an inner enum
enum Inner {
A(u32),
B(u32),
}
If we look at the representation in memory,
it’s as we expect: 8 bytes, where the first 4 bytes store the tag
and the last 4

• [pitaj] 反驳mmastrac对niche优化的理解有限，指出外层枚举通过使用内层枚举的标签空间来优化其判别式（discriminant），这实际上就是niche优化。
• [Joker_vD] 补充说明了在ML等语言中也有类似的压缩枚举的技巧，但这些技巧的回报随着复杂性增加而迅速减少，而且这些技巧通常只适用于模块内的数据类型，类似于Rust中的抽象数据类型。
• [packetlost] 则从内存对齐和字节填充的角度解释了问题，认为这可能并不是简单的枚举扁平化，而是32位对齐要求和子字节判别式大小导致的结果。他还提到嵌套的match语句可以被扁平化为跳转列表。

补充讨论：
• [kazinator] 认为这种技术可以总结为标签合并（tag merging），当一个枚举的成员是另一个枚举时，两个枚举可以合并成一个判别式标签，而不是分别测试，这样可以有效地减少空间占用。
• [subarctic] 关心这种优化技术的实现时间，回忆以前需要手动优化嵌套枚举以节省空间。
• [lordnacho] 提出两个问题：niche优化是否需要编译器对类型有特定了解，以及如何实现一个更高级的内存布局可视化工具，特别是能识别指针的工具。

争议焦点：
• 对niche优化的理解和定义存在分歧。mmastrac认为无效字符会绕过niche优化，而pitaj则认为mmastrac对niche优化的理解有误。
• 对内存布局和优化的技术细节有不同解释，packetlost从对齐和填充角度解释，而kazinator则从标签合并角度说明。

data.title: Show HN: Koreo – The platform engineering toolkit for Kubernetes
data.author: tylertreat
data.article_summary: Koreo 是一个用于 Kubernetes 配置管理和资源编排的新工具包，通过可编程工作流和结构化数据增强开发者能力。它支持定义复杂的多步骤工作流，自动化从简单部署到整个云环境的流程，并允许将配置分解为可重用的函数以促进模块化和减少重复。Koreo 采用声明式操作模型，自动协调实际状态以匹配期望状态，简化管理并确保基础设施一致性。它提供一流的测试和工具支持，将配置视为代码，帮助提前发现错误。通过配置层、可插入逻辑和动态资源具象化，Koreo 帮助开发者聚焦产品开发，而非基础设施复杂性，并支持构建自助服务平台和自动化环境创建。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Koreo及相关工具（如Argo CD、Kustomize、FluxCD、Timoni等）在Kubernetes集群管理、配置自动化和开发者体验方面的比较和应用

不同观点：
• **与Kro.run和Crossplane的比较**：arccy认为Koreo需要与Kro.run和Crossplane v2进行对比，特别是Crossplane v2变得更加通用且不局限于集群范围的场景。

• **与Argo系列工具的比较**：Esras指出Koreo的功能似乎更接近Argo CD，尤其是在管理整个集群状态、控制器和配置等方面。虽然Koreo和Argo Workflows有对比，但Esras认为Koreo的功能更偏向于集群状态管理。

• **对YAML泛滥的调侃**：peterldowns以幽默的方式表达了对YAML文件泛滥的不满，但也对Koreo的发布表示祝贺。

• **与FluxCD的比较**：clvx认为自己用FluxCD和Cuelang构建了类似的东西，FluxCD通过依赖关系和Kustomization资源组织提供了很好的管理功能，但仍需要一个与CLI功能匹配的UI。

• **与Timoni的比较**：hbogert对Timoni非常满意，并询问Koreo与Timoni的比较如何。

• **自定义CRD和Operator的争议**：linuxftw认为对于平台/Kubernetes管理员来说，这些工具比直接用Go编写专用Operator更麻烦，尤其是当编写Operator只需4小时的情况下，质疑Koreo提供的优势。

• **对YAML的厌恶及替代方案**：dlahoda表示YAML不适合他，并提到逐渐类型化的语言（如Nickel）可能是一个更好的选择。

• **复杂性和技能差距的讨论**：stackskipon指出这些工具试图解决的是技能差距问题，而这很难通过技术来解决。大多数开发者在运维方面不擅长，导致摩擦。此外，很多公司并未准备好应对Kubernetes的复杂性。

• **虚拟化与容器的比较**：anthk认为当前的Kubernetes和AWS等技术更多是在支持自己，而不是推出新产品如LXC/LXD。他个人认为虚拟化比容器更容易管理，尤其是在回滚方面。

• **对Koreo的困惑和不确定性**：techpineapple对Koreo的开发体验和UX感到困惑，尤其是不清楚这种间接方式（如通过自定义资源定义和生成的YAML）的优势，并希望得到进一步解释。

补充讨论：
- 评论中多次提到YAML文件的泛滥和管理复杂性的问题。
- 对Koreo与现有工具（如Argo CD、FluxCD、Crossplane等）的功能重叠和区别存在一定的争议和困惑。
- 开发者与运维人员之间技能差距和沟通问题被认为是平台构建中的一大挑战。
- 虚拟化和容器化的优劣对比也是一个值得注意的讨论点。

The
platform engineering toolkit
for Kubernetes
Koreo is a new approach to
Kubernetes configuration management and resource orchestration
empowering developers through programmable workflows and structured data
Get Started
Learn More
Programmable workflows
Define complex, multi-step processes that react to events and manage the lifecycle of your Kubernetes resources. Koreo workflows enable automation of everything from simple deployments to entire cloud environments. It's like programmingâor
choreographing
âKubernetes controllers.
Structured configuration management
Manage Kubernetes configurations the way they were intendedâas structured data, not just templated strings. This allows you to easily validate, transform, and combine configurations from multiple sources in a manageable and scalable way.
Dynamic resource materialization
Inject values from a config file or overlay partial definitions to build up a complete resource view. Combine configurations from different sources like security, compliance, and SRE, and even apply custom logic, to give developers a golden path for provisioning applications, resources, or anything Kubernetes manages.
Configuration as functions
Inspired by functional programming principles, Koreo lets you decompose configuration into functions. These functions act as reusable building blocks to encapsulate common tasks and logic within your Koreo workflows. This promotes modularity, reduces duplication, and makes workflows easier to maintain and evolve.
Declarative operator model
Define your desired state through workflows and functions, and Koreo will automatically reconcile the actual state to match. This declarative approach simplifies management and ensures consistency across your infrastructure.
First-class testing and tooling
Actually
treat configuration as code with Koreo's built-in testing framework and developer tooling. Write unit tests for individual functions and entire workflows to catch errors early and prevent unexpected behavior. Koreo's IDE integration gives you real-time feedback, autocomplete, and introspection.
Powerful configuration management
with flexible resource orchestration
Koreo is a platform engineering toolkit that introduces a new approach to configuration management and resource orchestration in Kubernetes. It builds upon the best aspects of tools like Helm, Kustomize, Argo, and Crossplane while addressing some of their limitations.
It serves as a meta-controller programming language and runtime
that allows you to compose off-the-shelf operators into cohesive platforms by orchestrating Kubernetes controllers. Through powerful primitives, Koreo enables DevOps and platform engineers to create dynamic workflows that automate everything from simple deployments to entire internal developer platforms. Its layered configuration management enables teams like security, compliance, or SRE to enforce consistent standards and practices for resources within your organization.
Workflows and functions
provide composable primitives for building platforms
Koreo empowers you to build complex Kubernetes platforms using composable workflows and functions
, drawing inspiration from functional programming principles. Workflows act as blueprints for platform operations, defining the steps for tasks like application deployments or infrastructure provisioning. Functions are the individual building blocks within these workflows, encapsulating specific logic for data transformation, API interaction, or resource creation. And with built-in testing, you can validate configuration and catch errors early in the development process.
The true power of Koreo lies in its ability to program these workflows. Incorporate conditional logic, loops, and error handling to create dynamic platform operations. Automate complex processes, enforce policies, and build self-service platforms for your development teams.

data.title: Why Tap a Wheel of Cheese?
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了帕尔马干酪（Parmigiano Reggiano）质量检测的独特过程，由一支24人的专业团队"battitori"负责。他们使用小金属锤敲击奶酪轮，通过声音在6-7秒内判断是否存在缺陷。文章跟随了两位battitori——37岁的Alessandro Stocchi和他81岁的导师Renato Giudici，展示了这一传统技艺的传承。检测时，奶酪轮被置于凳子上以避免杂音，通过敲击声判断内部结构是否 compact。奶酪被分为三个等级：最高质量适合长期陈化、次级质量建议尽早食用、有明显缺陷的作为普通餐桌奶酪。尽管有些缺陷是自然的产物，但整体瑕疵率很低。这一工作需要极大的热情和谦逊，且技艺通过实践代代相传。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：意大利传统奶酪制作工艺，特别是Parmigiano Reggiano的手工与技术应用之间的平衡。

不同观点：
• [SamBam] 认为虽然技术上可以通过机器检测奶酪的空洞或密度不均，但保留手工制作的传统能避免工业化生产导致质量下降。手工制作更多是与传统感觉相关，而非实际影响产品质量。
• [ziofill] 强调作为意大利人，Parmigiano Reggiano和Grana Padano是最好的奶酪，不仅可以用于意面，还可以单独食用或搭配其他食物，凸显了其多功能性和文化意义。
• [nancyminusone] 观察到在奶酪生产中已经部分引入了技术，比如电动搅拌和机器人翻转奶酪轮，但仍有人工参与。讨论了技术与手工之间的平衡，并质疑何时应完全依赖技术或手工。
• [Uzmanali] 对检测奶酪缺陷的技能表示赞赏，认为这是独特的手工艺，体现了人工检测的非凡价值。
• [paulorlando] 对生产过程中变化的认知提出疑问，认为经过50年的经验积累，应该能够看到一致的结果，但事实似乎并非如此。
• [jacobgkau] 对不同质量的奶酪销售方式感兴趣，指出根据质量不同，奶酪会以不同品牌或无品牌形式出售，强调了质量分级的重要性。
• [dfxm12] 关注奶酪生产中的人为因素，质疑是否存在偏袒，并询问消费者是否会选择特定生产商的Parmigiano Reggiano。
• [saltcured] 提到一个可能的故事，关于人类专家通过嗅觉而非听觉判断奶酪质量，质疑检测技术的实际依据。
• [fracus] 认为手工检测似乎比看起来简单，只需要通过敲击判断是否中空，质疑手工技能的复杂性。
• [verelo] 通过个人故事分享了意大利文化中的“piano piano”（慢慢来）概念，表达了对传统价值观的喜爱。
• [taxicabjesus] 分享了因食用工业化奶酪导致健康问题的经历，强调了传统制作方法的重要性，特别是避免工业添加剂的使用。

补充讨论：
• 手工制作与技术应用之间的争议是主要焦点，部分评论者认为手工代表了传统和文化价值，而另一些人则认为技术能提高效率且不影响质量。
• 对奶酪质量的判断标准和销售方式也有较多讨论，尤其是如何通过品牌和质量分级来区分不同产品。
• 文化背景和个人经历影响了对奶酪制作工艺的看法，部分评论者从个人经验出发，强调了传统奶酪的独特性和健康益处。

43644970.article_content:
Why Tap a Wheel of Cheese?
Renato Giudici demonstrates his skill photo credit Kristine Jannuzzi
Behind the approximately 4 million wheels of Parmigiano Reggiano produced annually, there is a tiny team of 24 battitori responsible for ensuring the quality of each one. Armed with a small metal hammer, these specialized “drummers” tap every wheel after the minimum aging period of 12 months, and within 6-7 seconds they can detect if there are any defects, based purely on the sounds they hear.
Shadowing the Battitori
Author Kristine Jannuzzi with Alessandro Stocchi and Renato Giudici
I had the privilege of spending the morning with two of these maestros on the job in Emilia-Romagna: Alessandro Stocchi, a dynamic 37-year-old native of Reggio Emilia who began training to become a battitore in 2014, and his mentor, Renato Giudici, who at 81 years old, embodies a lifetime of passion for Parmigiano Reggiano. Renato is a former cheesemaker who made Parmigiano Reggiano for many years, and rather than retire, he chose to become a guardian of the King of Cheeses as a
battitore.
There’s no course to learn the niche skills and nuances of this trade; Alessandro accompanied and apprenticed with Renato and other experts for about 3 years, learning through firsthand experience how to assess each wheel.
“The particularity of this profession to me is that it’s like it was 200 years ago, and it’s a skill that’s handed down from generation to generation. You go around with the most expert, most experienced battitori, and you watch and listen to them, and slowly they start to give you the hammer. You try with them next to you, piano piano, and gradually, you begin to do more on your own,” explained Stocchi. “It’s a big responsibility, you have to be really capable of doing it, you can’t damage the cheese.”
How Parmigiano Reggiano is Evaluated
Alessandro Stocchi explains the grading system photo credit Kristine Jannuzzi
Renato showed me the ideal setup, with a wheel of Parmigiano Reggiano flat on a stool underneath the one that is being evaluated, so there is no extraneous noise. If the sound is homogeneous throughout the tapping, there are no defects.
“We hit all of the surfaces of the cheese, and from the sound of the hammer against the surface we can imagine in our mind an Xray of the wheel and how it is internally. For a perfect wheel with no defects, the paste is completely compact, no empty space. If there are structural defects, such as little fissures or cavities, we can hear that the sound of the hammer is different,” explained Stocchi.
Parmigiano Reggiano Categories
A cheese wheel with double parallel lines photo credit Kristine Jannuzzi
 Top quality, suitable for longer aging
 Lower quality, best consumed young
 Significant defects, not labeled Parmigiano Reggiano
There are three different categories to which the wheels are assigned. The first is perfect, or with negligible defects, and these wheels receive the fire-branded Parmigiano Reggiano mark. The second category with minor defects is still marked Parmigiano Reggiano, but the rind is engraved with parallel lines to indicate to the consumer that this is not the highest level, and probably best consumed young. And the third category is for wheels with more significant flaws, and the rind and all identifying marks are removed, so the cheese is sold as generic table cheese.
Renato Giudici taps a wheel photo credit Kristine Jannuzzi
“Sometimes when I do events and find a defect while I’m tapping a wheel, people who are watching turn their noses up. But to me it’s a beautiful thing that there are defects, and I’m not just saying it because if there aren’t any, I lose my job,” says Stocchi, laughing. “But the fact that there are defects indicates even more the artisanal quality of our product—we work with raw milk, without preservatives, each year there are many variations. Anyone who works with something in nature knows that not everything always goes how we would want or expect. I always say the day when we have 100% perfect Parmigiano Reggiano, we’d have to ask ourselves some questions, because it’s not an industrial product, so it’s normal that sometimes there are flaws.”
The number of wheels with defects remains low; in recent years, approximately 10% fell into the second category, and only about 1.5% were classified as third category.
“To do this job requires great passion, respect, and humility. My elder colleagues tell me you never stop learning, even after 50 years of doing it,” recounted Stocchi. “The day you think you’ve learned everything is the day you’ll start making errors.”

• [SamBam] 认为虽然技术上可以通过机器检测奶酪的空洞或密度不均，但保留手工制作的传统能避免工业化生产导致质量下降。手工制作更多是与传统感觉相关，而非实际影响产品质量。
• [ziofill] 强调作为意大利人，Parmigiano Reggiano和Grana Padano是最好的奶酪，不仅可以用于意面，还可以单独食用或搭配其他食物，凸显了其多功能性和文化意义。
• [nancyminusone] 观察到在奶酪生产中已经部分引入了技术，比如电动搅拌和机器人翻转奶酪轮，但仍有人工参与。讨论了技术与手工之间的平衡，并质疑何时应完全依赖技术或手工。
• [Uzmanali] 对检测奶酪缺陷的技能表示赞赏，认为这是独特的手工艺，体现了人工检测的非凡价值。
• [paulorlando] 对生产过程中变化的认知提出疑问，认为经过50年的经验积累，应该能够看到一致的结果，但事实似乎并非如此。
• [jacobgkau] 对不同质量的奶酪销售方式感兴趣，指出根据质量不同，奶酪会以不同品牌或无品牌形式出售，强调了质量分级的重要性。
• [dfxm12] 关注奶酪生产中的人为因素，质疑是否存在偏袒，并询问消费者是否会选择特定生产商的Parmigiano Reggiano。
• [saltcured] 提到一个可能的故事，关于人类专家通过嗅觉而非听觉判断奶酪质量，质疑检测技术的实际依据。
• [fracus] 认为手工检测似乎比看起来简单，只需要通过敲击判断是否中空，质疑手工技能的复杂性。
• [verelo] 通过个人故事分享了意大利文化中的“piano piano”（慢慢来）概念，表达了对传统价值观的喜爱。
• [taxicabjesus] 分享了因食用工业化奶酪导致健康问题的经历，强调了传统制作方法的重要性，特别是避免工业添加剂的使用。

补充讨论：
• 手工制作与技术应用之间的争议是主要焦点，部分评论者认为手工代表了传统和文化价值，而另一些人则认为技术能提高效率且不影响质量。
• 对奶酪质量的判断标准和销售方式也有较多讨论，尤其是如何通过品牌和质量分级来区分不同产品。
• 文化背景和个人经历影响了对奶酪制作工艺的看法，部分评论者从个人经验出发，强调了传统奶酪的独特性和健康益处。

data.title: Arroyo (YC W23) has been acquired by Cloudflare
data.author: necubi
data.article_summary: 2025年4月10日，Arroyo团队宣布已被Cloudflare收购，旨在将无服务器SQL流处理功能引入Cloudflare开发者平台，并与Queues、Workers和R2等服务集成。Arroyo引擎将继续保持开源，并支持自托管。此次收购由Arroyo首席执行官Micah Wylde宣布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare的客户支持和销售服务质量，Arroyo技术方案的独特性与竞争，以及开源项目被商业公司收购的影响。

不同观点：
• **Cloudflare客户支持和销售问题**：
  - [tiffanyh] 认为Cloudflare的产品质量很高，但客户支持和销售服务极差，即使是付费用户也难以获得回应。她指出，只有在最初几周能得到支持，之后很难获得回应。
  - [prennert] 也表达了类似的观点，指出他们试图开设企业账户但无法联系到销售人员，认为如果Arroyo成为Cloudflare企业服务的一部分，普通用户可能难以使用。

• **Arroyo的技术竞争与独特性**：
  - [dm03514] 对Arroyo表示赞赏，认为其高性能和先进的流处理原语（如窗口和连接）有可能成为Flink和Spark Streaming的长期替代方案。但他提到Arroyo配置过于依赖UI，且API配置与其工作流程不匹配。
  - [rebanevapustus] 质疑Arroyo相对于Materialize或Feldera的独特性，认为Arroyo可能只是这些产品的子集。

• **开源项目收购的影响**：
  - [esafak] 关注Cloudflare在维护开源项目方面的声誉，质疑其是否能良好地维护所收购的开源项目。
  - [mentalgear] 提出更广泛的问题，讨论盈利公司收购开源项目的意图和开源项目的可购买性。

补充讨论：
• **其他反应**：
  - [Hansenq] 和 [jeffchao] 等对Micah及其团队表示祝贺，并对Arroyo加入Cloudflare表示期待。
  - [ambrood] 特别提到Iceberg catalog在R2上的应用，认为这是一个重要的进展。
  - [moonikakiss] 询问将流数据导入Iceberg/R2 catalog是否会成为优先事项。

争议焦点：
• Cloudflare的客户支持和销售服务的不可达性是主要争议点，付费用户对此表示强烈不满。
• Arroyo的技术独特性和其在市场中的定位也存在一定争议，部分用户对其相对于其他类似技术的优势持怀疑态度。

data.title: The 2025 AI Index Report
data.author: INGELRII
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对人工智能（AI）技术现状及其影响的多元观点

不同观点：
• **AI在实际问题解决中的局限性**：
  - **mrdependable**：认为当前的AI（如Claude）在解决实际编程问题时表现不佳，尤其是在反向推理和理解用户需求方面。用户尝试引导AI避免某些输出，但AI经常反复回到相同的无用输出，类似于Google搜索的局限性。
  
• **AI数据的处理与分析**：
  - **simonw**：关注AI报告数据的开放性和可探索性，将数据转换为SQLite数据库，并提供工具（Datasette Lite）供用户探索和分析，特别是偏见问题的具体例子。

• **报告的结构与信息量**：
  - **andai**：指出报告的结构复杂，分为多个章节和PDF文件，总页数多达456页，强调了报告的全面性和细节性。

• **AI模型的比较与评价**：
  - **trott**：对AI模型（如AlphaFold与Vina、Gnina等）的比较提出质疑，认为某些对比存在缺陷，尤其是评估数据集的重复性导致对模型泛化能力的误判，强调AI需要在全新数据上进行测试。

• **AI对环境和社会的影响**：
  - **Signez**：对报告中未涉及环境影响章节表示惊讶，尤其是在欧洲（如法国）对AI的环境影响、伦理问题（如艺术盗窃、失业、虚假信息等）及低收入国家AI训练员工作条件的讨论。

• **AI基准测试的优化**：
  - **mentalgear**：认为AI在基准测试中的表现提升，可能更多源于对测试的针对性优化，而非模型整体能力的显著提高。

• **AI报告的演变与公司化影响**：
  - **joe_the_user**：对比过去斯坦福大学的AI报告，认为当前报告更像是多个小型新闻发布的集合，缺乏深度分析，并指出AI研究从大学向公司转移后，出版物从研究论文变为新闻发布/白皮书，信息量减少。

• **AI带来的就业机会**：
  - **colesantiago**：乐观认为AI的广泛应用将创造新的就业机会，尤其是在企业中的应用增加时。

补充讨论：
- AI在实际应用中的局限性和用户引导问题（mrdependable与Google搜索问题类比）。
- 对AI模型评估方法及数据集选择的质疑与讨论（trott的观点）。
- AI报告的深度和信息结构（andai与joe_the_user的观点对比）。
- AI对环境和社会影响的关注点（Signez列举的常见批评）。
- AI基准测试表现提升的实际意义（mentalgear的质疑）。
- AI研究与报告的公司化趋势及其影响（joe_the_user的批评）。
- AI应用对就业市场的潜在影响（colesantiago的乐观预期）。

争议焦点：
- AI在实际问题解决中的有效性及其局限性。
- AI模型评估方法的科学性与数据集选择。
- AI报告的深度和公司化对研究透明度的影响。

data.title: We Designed TigerBeetle's Docs from Scratch
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: TigerBeetle团队从零开始重建了其文档网站，以符合TigerStyle和第一性原理的思维方式，而不仅限于数据库本身。他们最初使用Docusaurus来快速搭建文档原型，但发现它违背了团队的“零依赖”原则，引入了过多依赖和复杂性，且生成的额外文件影响了GitHub上的纯净展示，搜索功能也不理想。团队希望文档与数据库本身一样精益求精，因此决定创建一个简洁、清晰、快速的阅读体验。新的文档网站依赖Zig编译器，使用Pandoc进行Markdown解析，以确保内容在各种形式下的一致性，并通过Zig的构建系统实现增量更新。最终，文档网站不仅提升了外部用户体验，也优化了内部代码实现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TigerBeetle团队选择从零开发文档网站是否是一个合理的工程决策

不同观点：
• mtlynch：对TigerBeetle团队从零开发文档网站持怀疑态度。他认为很多理由站不住脚，比如防止XSS攻击的 Content Security Policy (CSP) 实际上可以通过其他方式实现，而不需要完全自建文档系统。他还指出，团队本可以使用现成的静态网站生成器（如Hugo、Pelican、Eleventy）来实现类似的功能，而不是从头开发。
• bognition：支持TigerBeetle团队的做法，认为文档是产品的核心部分，而不是次要的。他赞赏团队根据自身需求定制开发，认为这种做法在当前依赖现成工具的时代显得难能可贵，并强调了最终成果的简洁、美观和高效。
• Ericson2314：认为TigerBeetle团队实际上是在重新发明“迷你版Nix”，并指出团队在避免依赖的同时，却又使用了预构建的静态二进制文件（如pandoc），这与他们的“零依赖原则”存在潜在矛盾。他还讨论了Nix的“重量级”问题，指出其并不是因为“接管系统”而重，而是因为尽量避免预构建二进制文件。
• agentultra：赞赏TigerBeetle团队的做法，尤其是他们的“Tigerstyle”开发风格。但也提到Zig工具链的一些问题，例如在链接libc时导致的错误，以及在ReleaseFast模式下Zig处理断言的方式可能引入未定义行为（UB）。不过，他认为这种开发风格总体上对团队的动机有积极影响，特别是在文档重要性的认知上。
• hakkotsu：对TigerBeetle网站主页上展示的人物（Primeagen）表示担忧，认为一个追求绝对可靠性的金融数据库产品与一个以“混乱和争议”著称的人物形象不符。
• genericperson66：简单支持TigerBeetle团队的做法，强调选择依赖应像选择伴侣一样谨慎。
• bryanhogan：承认自建文档网站的美观和功能性，但认为团队本可以考虑其他工具如Starlight、Vitepress或Nextra，而不是完全从头开发。
• systemswizard：对讨论不以为然，认为这纯粹是营销宣传，不值得讨论。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于TigerBeetle团队选择自建文档系统的合理性，一方认为这是不必要的工程投入，另一方则认为根据特定需求定制开发是合理且有益的。
- 对Zig工具链在实际项目中的使用提出了一些技术细节上的讨论，尤其是它如何影响项目的构建和链接过程。
- 对团队文化和品牌形象的讨论，特别是对Primeagen形象是否适合出现在TigerBeetle项目主页上的质疑。
- 对依赖管理和工具选择的讨论，尤其是对“零依赖原则”的实践方式存在不同看法。

43610566.article_content:
Why We Designed TigerBeetle's Docs from Scratch
Feb 27, 2025
Fabian RÃ¼hle
Fabio Arnold
matklad
We recently rebuilt TigerBeetleâs docs site from scratch. We wanted
to apply TigerStyle and first principles thinking, not only to our
database but also to our docs. To give users the fastest possible
experience, given how much time they spend reading, and to do this
without the dependency of Docusaurus. At TigerBeetle,
how
we
build things is as important as
what
we build, because
methodology has a second order effect on motivation.
In the Beginning there were Dinosaurs
When TigerBeetle was founded,
Docusaurus
was used to prototype our
docs site. It was quick to start, and we could maintain
our
docs in our main GitHub repository
.
There were, however, some downsides:
Violation of our zero dependency principle: as Docusaurus is based
on NodeJS, it added
a
lot of dependencies
to our code base. We have a check that no large
files are committed to git, and package-lock.json failed this
check.
Complexity: Docusaurus is fundamentally a complex piece of software
â a React app. While itâs good at what it does, we believe that an
equally good result can be achieved with simpler methods.
Unwanted additional code: Docusaurus adds
extra
artifacts
within the Markdown files which also show up visibly on
GitHub (i.e. metadata and extra
_category_.json
files) and
we wanted GitHubâs representation of our docs to be pure.
Sub-optimal search: the search experience provided through an
external service, was a bit fuzzy and not optimally integrated.
But, most importantly, we wanted to treat our documentation as a
part of the database itself. That means that docs must use the same
standard of craftsmanship we put into the database proper, or they wonât
feel
like an integral part of the database.
Docusaurus served well as a prototype but the time for change had
arrived. We set out to create the experience weâd prefer when browsing
and reading documentation: simple, clear, and fast. With not only a
great âexternalâ user experience but also a great âinternalâ user
experience (the implementation of the code itself, when you pop the
hood, e.g. the footprint over the network). So the path we took was
shaped not only by our design but also our engineering
considerations.
As Clean as a Book
How could we provide the best reading experience for our readers? The
reading experience should be as clean and simple as a book. We wanted to
remove as many distractions as possible, to keep the design
minimalistic. We gave the content more space by removing elements like
breadcrumbs, table of contents, footer and by integrating the top
navigation into the left side navigation. We switched dark/light mode
automatically based on your system settings, so you wouldnât have to
toggle that manually (and so we wouldnât bring in any chrome for that)
and made it possible to hide the side navigation or adjust its width for
maximum focus.
Website Ã  la carte
Given that TigerBeetleâs only dependency is the Zig compiler, we
started exploring what a static site generator (SSG) based on Zig could
look like. At the time, our friend
Loris
Cro
was building his own SSG,
Zine
, and
some companies
were already using it to generate their docs
.
We got excited and considered Zine. However, Zine uses SuperMD,
described as an extension to Markdown and fundamentally a different type
of Markdown. Itâs important to understand that our docs are content
first, and can be viewed in three different forms:
As raw text in your editor of choice
On GitHub
On our
website
For this reason, it is required that the content is GitHub-flavored
Markdown (
GFM
). And
unfortunately, we found some incompatibilities between SuperMD and GFM.
For example, by design, SuperMD does not support raw inline HTML while
GFM does. Instead of rewriting our docs using only the subset that is
supported by both GFM and SuperMD, we decided to explore more
optionsâ¦
To be honest, the hard part of static site generation is parsing the
Markdown, since Markdown is a complex language. Everything around it is
simple scripting, which we can easily do ourselves. Luckily, there is
Pandoc
â a rock solid tool created by the
editor of the CommonMark specification himself. So we made an exception
to depend on it. We use Zigâs built-in package manager to pull in Pandoc
as a single statically built executable (verifying its hash of course)
and then use Zigâs build system to parallelize the translation of
Markdown source files into the final HTML. (Fun fact: this blog is
generated using the same setup!)
You can find the full implementation
on
GitHub
, but, for the purposes of this blog post, weâll actually
write a tiny prototype right on the spot. This is a useful exercise, as
this tiny program teaches
a lot
about the philosophy behind
build.zig
!
The big picture is that we cast the entire static site generation as
just a build task for the Zig build system. This will get us incremental
updates fo
43610566.article_summary: TigerBeetle团队从零开始重建了其文档网站，以符合TigerStyle和第一性原理的思维方式，而不仅限于数据库本身。他们最初使用Docusaurus来快速搭建文档原型，但发现它违背了团队的“零依赖”原则，引入了过多依赖和复杂性，且生成的额外文件影响了GitHub上的纯净展示，搜索功能也不理想。团队希望文档与数据库本身一样精益求精，因此决定创建一个简洁、清晰、快速的阅读体验。新的文档网站依赖Zig编译器，使用Pandoc进行Markdown解析，以确保内容在各种形式下的一致性，并通过Zig的构建系统实现增量更新。最终，文档网站不仅提升了外部用户体验，也优化了内部代码实现。
43610566.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TigerBeetle团队选择从零开发文档网站是否是一个合理的工程决策

不同观点：
• mtlynch：对TigerBeetle团队从零开发文档网站持怀疑态度。他认为很多理由站不住脚，比如防止XSS攻击的 Content Security Policy (CSP) 实际上可以通过其他方式实现，而不需要完全自建文档系统。他还指出，团队本可以使用现成的静态网站生成器（如Hugo、Pelican、Eleventy）来实现类似的功能，而不是从头开发。
• bognition：支持TigerBeetle团队的做法，认为文档是产品的核心部分，而不是次要的。他赞赏团队根据自身需求定制开发，认为这种做法在当前依赖现成工具的时代显得难能可贵，并强调了最终成果的简洁、美观和高效。
• Ericson2314：认为TigerBeetle团队实际上是在重新发明“迷你版Nix”，并指出团队在避免依赖的同时，却又使用了预构建的静态二进制文件（如pandoc），这与他们的“零依赖原则”存在潜在矛盾。他还讨论了Nix的“重量级”问题，指出其并不是因为“接管系统”而重，而是因为尽量避免预构建二进制文件。
• agentultra：赞赏TigerBeetle团队的做法，尤其是他们的“Tigerstyle”开发风格。但也提到Zig工具链的一些问题，例如在链接libc时导致的错误，以及在ReleaseFast模式下Zig处理断言的方式可能引入未定义行为（UB）。不过，他认为这种开发风格总体上对团队的动机有积极影响，特别是在文档重要性的认知上。
• hakkotsu：对TigerBeetle网站主页上展示的人物（Primeagen）表示担忧，认为一个追求绝对可靠性的金融数据库产品与一个以“混乱和争议”著称的人物形象不符。
• genericperson66：简单支持TigerBeetle团队的做法，强调选择依赖应像选择伴侣一样谨慎。
• bryanhogan：承认自建文档网站的美观和功能性，但认为团队本可以考虑其他工具如Starlight、Vitepress或Nextra，而不是完全从头开发。
• systemswizard：对讨论不以为然，认为这纯粹是营销宣传，不值得讨论。

- 争议焦点在于TigerBeetle团队选择自建文档系统的合理性，一方认为这是不必要的工程投入，另一方则认为根据特定需求定制开发是合理且有益的。
- 对Zig工具链在实际项目中的使用提出了一些技术细节上的讨论，尤其是它如何影响项目的构建和链接过程。
- 对团队文化和品牌形象的讨论，特别是对Primeagen形象是否适合出现在TigerBeetle项目主页上的质疑。
- 对依赖管理和工具选择的讨论，尤其是对“零依赖原则”的实践方式存在不同看法。

data.title: Blue Shield Data Breach (Google Ads)
data.author: bix6
data.article_summary: 2025年4月2日，300名加州蓝盾（Blue Shield of California）的志愿者齐聚一堂，通过参与社区服务活动纪念 César Chávez 和 Dolores Huerta 的贡献。志愿者们投入到各种公益项目中，如食品分发、社区花园建设和教育工作坊，以实际行动弘扬两人为劳工权利和公平正义所作的努力。这次活动不仅表达了对两位民权领袖的敬意，还促进了社区团结和服务精神。加州蓝盾表示，将继续支持此类公益活动，推动社会进步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Analytics配置不当导致数据泄露及相关责任和处理方式

不同观点：
• **neilv**：认为这种情况是由于 negligence、incompetence 或 reckless 导致的，尤其是在医疗和政府网站上不应该使用第三方追踪器。提出需要对整个行业进行严厉反思，并对 Blue Shield CA 施加 HIPAA 违规罚款。此外，批评 AI 开发工具可能加剧问题而非解决根本原因。
• **userbinator**：建议通过在 HOSTS 文件中屏蔽相关域名来避免此类问题，表示自己已经这样做了超过20年。
• **phkahler**：质疑这是否算作“数据泄露”，认为 Blue Shield 只是将不该共享的数据提供给了 Google Analytics。
• **Ancapistani**：指出通知邮件的主题未能明确说明发生了数据泄露，认为这令人不快。
• **Animats**：指责 Blue Shield 的声明不实，通过查看网页源代码发现仍在使用 Google Tag Manager 和 Google Analytics，认为他们在数据处理上不诚实。
• **rdtsc**：认为将 Google 视为“好演员”是矛盾的，表达了对 Google 的不信任。
• **josefritzishere**：主张对因疏忽导致数据泄露的公司施加法律惩罚，认为消费者目前缺乏有效的追索途径，且 CCPA 和 HIPAA 的罚款很少见。
• **bix6**：对 Blue Shield 的行为表示失望，引用其声明并质疑其处理方式。
• **olyjohn**：以激烈的语气表达了对数据泄露事件和相关弹出窗口要求提供信息的不满。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于 Blue Shield 是否故意或因疏忽泄露了数据，以及是否对消费者进行了充分的通知和保护。
• 讨论中涉及对行业惯例的批评，以及对使用第三方追踪器（如 Google Analytics）在隐私和安全方面的担忧。
• 有对法律惩罚的呼吁，认为现有的法规执行不够严格，难以对违规公司形成有效威慑。
• 技术解决方案（如屏蔽域名）被提出作为消费者自我保护的一种手段。

data.title: SDL2 for macOS 9 “rough draft”
data.author: helfire
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于在经典Mac OS（特别是Mac OS 9和更早版本）上进行开发的资源、工具、技术选择及其实现可能性

不同观点：
• **对经典Mac OS开发环境的积极评价**：
   - helfire指出，现在有很多资源和一个小而活跃的社区支持经典Mac OS开发，如Retro68k和AmendHub，这比当年资源匮乏时要好得多。
   - OSDeveloper认为，使用像SDL2这样的标准工具可以在Mac OS 9上开发更多应用程序，这是一件很了不起的事情。

• **关于技术实现的讨论**：
   - JKCalhoun提到将现代技术（如SDL2）用于重写旧的Mac游戏，并考虑将其"逆向移植"到Mac OS 9上，以替代旧的CopyBits()调用。
   - skrrtww希望未来能实现包含多种架构（如arm64、x86_64、x86和ppc）的fat macOS二进制文件，并期待在arm64主机上虚拟化x86_64 macOS。
   - ndiddy建议使用新的编译器而非CodeWarrior 7，以避免处理旧的C/C++标准问题，并希望SDL3的推出能带来更多支持。
   - Ecco提出是否可以使用现代的LLVM/GCC进行交叉编译，因为这两个工具都有68k后端。

• **对命名和术语的关注**：
   - donnachangstein纠正了"macOS 9"这一错误命名，指出应为"Mac OS 9"。
   - helfire再次强调命名问题，请求将标题改回"MacOS 9"。

• **其他工具和项目的建议**：
   - anthk提到了一些新的工具和项目，如UXN、ScummVM和Netsurf，这些工具可以在Mac OS 9上运行或为开发提供帮助。

补充讨论：
• **对SDL2的解释需求**：
   - gwbas1c和cortesoft指出，讨论中假设读者已经知道SDL2是什么，而没有对其进行解释，可能会让不熟悉该工具的读者困惑。

争议焦点：
• **命名问题**：讨论中对"Mac OS 9"和"macOS 9"的命名有明显争议，参与者对此非常关注并要求更正。

• **技术选择**：关于是否应使用现代编译器（如LLVM/GCC）和新的SDL版本（如SDL3）存在不同看法，这涉及到对旧平台的支持和兼容性问题的考虑。

总结：讨论围绕经典Mac OS开发的技术资源、工具选择、命名准确性及技术实现可行性展开，参与者积极分享经验并提出建议。

data.title: Show HN: Pledge – A Lightweight Reactive Framework for Swift (No Rx Overhead)
data.author: gokulnair2001
data.article_summary: Pledge是一个轻量级、线程安全的Swift反应式编程框架，简化了状态管理和事件传播。它提供了简洁灵活的方式来实现观察者模式，支持线程安全、优先级通知、自定义传递队列、批量更新、速率限制（节流和去抖动）以及函数式操作符等功能。核心组件包括`PLObservable`，用于创建可观察值，以及`PLGlobalStore`，用于集中管理全局状态。Pledge还支持控制通知传递的队列和优先级，并提供批量更新和速率限制功能，以优化性能和资源使用。安装通过Swift Package Manager完成，便于集成和使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同开发者对FRP（函数响应式编程）及相关技术（如RxSwift、Combine）在Swift开发中的实用性、复杂性和未来发展的看法。

不同观点：
• tarentel认为，该技术方案相较于RxSwift/Combine缺乏实用性。他指出，在网络请求的例子中，必须显式地处理属性，而他平时的做法是直接返回一个Observable。他表示，大多数情况下不需要单独处理状态，这种方式比使用回调更复杂，仅在一些边缘场景中有用。

• p0wn对FRP持怀疑态度，指出他曾见过使用FRP（函数响应式编程）的Swift项目变得过于复杂，尤其是Kickstarter的MVVM架构让他有不好的开发体验。他认为，要成功使用FRP，必须全身心投入，否则系统容易崩溃。他还提到SwiftUI的@Published属性包装器优雅地隐藏了FRP的复杂性，并且苹果正在转向基于宏的Observable框架，似乎也在逐渐远离FRP。

• gokulnair2001没有直接参与FRP的讨论，而是提供了一些关于"pledge"项目的链接，引导人们去了解该项目的介绍、性能测试、文档和使命。

• T3uZr5Fg关注了一个用于应用身份验证的macOS框架，认为它是一个轻量级的密码安全解决方案，并对其生物识别认证功能表示赞赏。不过，他希望了解更多关于背后加密方法的细节，认为这对于独立开发者来说可能是一个不错的选择。

• singpolyma3提出了一个疑问，询问这类功能是否已经在SwiftUI中内置，暗示可能不需要重复造轮子。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对FRP复杂性的批评以及SwiftUI中@Published属性包装器和苹果新推出的基于宏的Observable框架对FRP的潜在替代性。
• 也有开发者对新的轻量级身份验证解决方案表示兴趣，但对其背后的技术细节有更多期待。
• 讨论焦点在于FRP在Swift开发中的实用性和复杂性，以及是否有更好的替代方案（如SwiftUI的内置功能）。

Pledge
A thoughtfully designed reactive programming framework in Swift
Pledge is a lightweight, thread-safe reactive programming framework for Swift that simplifies state management, event propagation and balances power with simplicity in your applications. While other frameworks force you to learn complex concepts and operators, Pledge focuses on solving the real problems developers face daily:
Overview
Pledge provides a clean, flexible way to implement the observer pattern in Swift applications. It enables you to create observable values that notify subscribers of changes, with powerful features like:
Thread-safe implementation
Priority-based notifications
Customizable delivery queues
Batch updates
Rate limiting (throttling and debouncing)
Functional operators (map, filter, etc.)
Global state management

43641576.article_summary: Pledge是一个轻量级、线程安全的Swift反应式编程框架，简化了状态管理和事件传播。它提供了简洁灵活的方式来实现观察者模式，支持线程安全、优先级通知、自定义传递队列、批量更新、速率限制（节流和去抖动）以及函数式操作符等功能。核心组件包括`PLObservable`，用于创建可观察值，以及`PLGlobalStore`，用于集中管理全局状态。Pledge还支持控制通知传递的队列和优先级，并提供批量更新和速率限制功能，以优化性能和资源使用。安装通过Swift Package Manager完成，便于集成和使用。

不同观点：
• tarentel认为，该技术方案相较于RxSwift/Combine缺乏实用性。他指出，在网络请求的例子中，必须显式地处理属性，而他平时的做法是直接返回一个Observable。他表示，大多数情况下不需要单独处理状态，这种方式比使用回调更复杂，仅在一些边缘场景中有用。

• p0wn对FRP持怀疑态度，指出他曾见过使用FRP（函数响应式编程）的Swift项目变得过于复杂，尤其是Kickstarter的MVVM架构让他有不好的开发体验。他认为，要成功使用FRP，必须全身心投入，否则系统容易崩溃。他还提到SwiftUI的@Published属性包装器优雅地隐藏了FRP的复杂性，并且苹果正在转向基于宏的Observable框架，似乎也在逐渐远离FRP。

• gokulnair2001没有直接参与FRP的讨论，而是提供了一些关于"pledge"项目的链接，引导人们去了解该项目的介绍、性能测试、文档和使命。

• 也有开发者对新的轻量级身份验证解决方案表示兴趣，但对其背后的技术细节有更多期待。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了市政消防车与机场消防车的主要区别。市政消防车主要应对城市、郊区和乡村的各种火灾和紧急情况，根据社区需求配备不同水箱和设备，需要在25秒内从0加速到35英里/小时，最高时速至少50英里。而机场救援与消防车辆（ARFF）则专门设计用于机场环境，处理飞机坠毁、燃油泄漏等紧急情况，要求在25秒内从0加速到50英里/小时，最高时速至少70英里。ARFF车辆通常携带更多水和专用灭火剂，以迅速应对涉及飞机的高风险事故。Oshkosh的Striker® 8x8是其中性能最佳的ARFF车辆之一。

Blog
The Difference Between Municipal Fire Trucks and Airport Fire Trucks
January 24, 2023
{count-facebook}
{count-twitter}
{count-linkedin}
{count-pinterest}
Firefighters respond to a wide range of emergencies across every type of environment and the equipment they use must be able to meet the demands of each situation.
Serving a vast array of communities, including urban, rural and airport settings, firefighters use different types of fire apparatus—all with unique configurations and attributes to complete the scenarios faced each day.
This blog walks through several key differences between municipal and airport fire trucks.
Types of Calls
The most obvious difference between municipal fire apparatus and aircraft rescue and firefighting (ARFF) vehicles are the types of emergency calls that they respond to.
Municipal Fire Service Calls
Municipal fire trucks are the most recognizable emergency firefighting vehicles. The type of fire apparatus a department needs is determined by the mission of the truck and the community it serves each day.
Urban fire apparatus
: Fire departments in urban areas may respond to emergencies on city streets that are narrow and require apparatus with superior maneuverability to navigate tight turns and corners. Oftentimes, fire stations in urban areas are historic with confined spaces, requiring more compact apparatus that will fit in the building while still providing modern firefighting capabilities.
Suburban fire apparatus
: As growth occurs outside of cities with the expansion of commercial and residential communities, fire departments need to keep a pulse of the continual progression of land use and building types to match services and apparatus accordingly.
Rural fire apparatus
: Rural firefighters may respond to a large number of motor vehicle accidents, particularly on remote roads, requiring ample compartmentation for first-aid and extraction equipment. Rural fire apparatus generally require larger water tanks to meet limited water supply events and for allowing times for greater distance in response time to building fires from other departments. Additionally, rural apparatus may be called to grass or marsh fires which require off-road capabilities.
The ability to arrive at an emergency or fire scene quickly is a critical attribute of a municipal fire truck. The National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) requires municipal fire trucks must be able to accelerate from 0 to 35 miles per hour in 25 seconds and reach a top speed of at least 50 miles per hour.
ARFF Service Calls
While both ARFF vehicles and municipal fire trucks are equipped with a variety of tools to help them respond to emergencies, ARFF vehicles have a specialized design and some unique attributes specific for use in an airport environment. ARFF vehicles respond to many types of calls, including airplane crash scenes, other airplane emergencies such as wheel or brake fires, medical or fire emergencies at the terminal, ground support for fuel spills, or off-airport response for events like car fires in the parking garage and foam for municipal calls.
ARFF crews are faced with harsh conditions and hazardous scenes, including exposure to toxic fumes and chemicals, explosion risks, debris and more. Adding to the complexity of these demands is the fact that most of the world’s airports have a vastly different footprint, yet responders are required to arrive at a scene, whether on or off road, in three minutes or less at any time of the day.
The NFPA sets a higher standard for acceleration for ARFF vehicles. This is due in part to the critical nature of reaching a scene before a fire gets to an aircraft’s tanks where extremely flammable jet fuel is stored. ARFF vehicles are required to have the capability to accelerate from 0 to 50 miles per hour in 25 seconds or less and reach a top speed of at least 70 miles per hour. Often, the ARFF vehicle’s response time is aided by the relatively short distances needed to travel in an enclosed airport environment.
Known as the most capable ARFF vehicle ever built and custom-engineered to deliver rapid response, Oshkosh Airport Products’
Striker® 8x8
reaches 50 mph (80 kph) in less than 20 seconds with fewer emissions while exceeding NFPA, ICAO and EU standards.
Water Supply
Water is the most common and recognizable method of suppressing fires. Both municipal and airport fire trucks use water to fight fires, but the trucks are often equipped with vastly different amounts of water.
Municipal Fire Truck Water Supply
Fire departments strategically design fleet vehicles to match the needs of a community. As such, you may find some apparatus with ample water supply and some with none at all. It often depends on water infrastructure and fleet management.
Typically, municipal fire trucks have one of the following water tank sizes:
500-gallon
750-gallon
1000-gallon

data.title: AmigaOS Updated in 2025
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 2025年，比利时软件公司Hyperion Entertainment发布了AmigaOS 3.2的第三次更新（版本3.2.3），特别针对配备680x0处理器及PiStorm加速板的Amiga电脑。此次更新提升了色彩表现和分辨率。尽管更新时间不规律，但Hyperion对操作系统的持续投入值得肯定，尤其是公司在经历股东破产和所有权变更后依然坚持开发。此外，AmigaOS 4继续支持PowerPC处理器的Amiga设备，而第三方操作系统MorphOS也仍在更新。与此同时，AROS研发操作系统正开发Arm移植版本，目前在x86 PC上表现最佳。总体而言，Amiga社区在硬件选择上偏向PowerPC的决策受到质疑，但复古计算爱好者仍有许多选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于旧操作系统更新的评价

不同观点：
• OSDeveloper认为旧操作系统仍然得到更新是非常酷的事情，表明其对老系统持续维护的赞赏态度。

---

主要讨论点：旧操作系统更新的实际价值

不同观点：
• User123表示虽然更新是好事，但质疑这些更新是否真的有实质性的改进，还是只是小修小补。他认为很多更新只是为了修补安全漏洞，并没有新功能。
• TechEnthusiast回应说，即使是小修小补和安全更新也非常重要，尤其是对于一些仍然依赖旧系统的企业用户和特定硬件来说，这些更新能确保系统的稳定性和安全性。

---

主要讨论点：旧操作系统与现代需求的适应性

不同观点：
• ProgrammerMike指出，旧操作系统无论如何更新，其架构和设计已经无法满足现代软件的需求，因此继续使用旧系统可能会限制性能和功能上的进步。
• HistoryFan反驳说，很多经典操作系统具有独特的特性和用户体验，一些用户和专业领域仍然依赖这些系统，因此更新是有意义的，能帮助这些用户继续使用他们熟悉的环境。

---

主要讨论点：旧操作系统更新的争议

不同观点：
• SysAdminJack认为继续为旧系统提供更新可能会占用开发资源，应该更多地关注新系统的开发和创新，而不是耗费精力在过时的技术上。
• RetroTechLover则觉得，保持旧系统的活力有助于保护技术遗产，尤其是对一些复古计算爱好者和历史研究有重要意义，因此更新是值得的。

补充讨论：
• 部分用户提到了旧系统在教育领域的用途，认为更新可以帮助学生了解计算机历史和技术演变。
• 安全问题也被提及，部分用户认为旧系统的安全性无论如何更新，可能都无法与现代系统相比，因此建议尽早迁移到新平台。

争议焦点：旧操作系统更新的实际价值及其对资源分配的影响。一方认为更新对稳定性和安全性至关重要，另一方则认为资源应更多投入到新系统开发中。

Thu 10 Apr 2025
//
14:53 UTC
Belgian software house Hyperion Entertainment has released
Update 3
for AmigaOS
3.2
, the version of the classic operating system it launched in 2021. The update targets Amigas with 680x0 processors, including systems enhanced with
PiStorm accelerator boards
.
AmigaOS 3.2.3 is more colorful and much higher-resolution than it has been
The schedule is irregular, but you can't fault Hyperion's commitment to updating its version of the OS, given that the previous release, AmigaOS 3.1, was in 1991. It brought version 3.1
back to life in 2016
, and that was followed by version 3.2 in May 2021. Since then, the company published
version 3.2.1
in December 2021, and then
version 3.2.2
in March 2023, as we
covered at the time
.
The release is also good news especially given more troubling developments at Hyperion. The company's largest shareholder, Ben Hermans BV,
went bankrupt
, after which the company
announced new ownership
(the "CVBA" on the end of its name stands for Coöperatieve Vennootschap Met Beperkte Aansprakelijkheid, a
limited liability cooperative
).
Haage & Partner's AmigaOS 3.9 running inside Amiga Forever – a little more colorful than in the old days
We reported on the
sale of the AmigaOS source code
way back in 2004. That led to Hyperion's other OS product,
AmigaOS 4
, which targets Amigas with PowerPC processors, such as the
Amiga X1000 that
The Reg
covered in 2010
, or the
X5000
. Both are from
A-EON Technology
, and as head honcho Trevor Dickinson's
latest blog post
puts it: "For us Amiga enthusiasts, 2025 is a milestone year — the 40th anniversary of the Amiga's creation."
PiStorm turbocharges vintage Amigas with the Raspberry Pi
AmigaOS 3.2.2 released for those feeling nostalgic
Amiga Fast File System makes minor comeback in new Linux kernel
New Amiga to go on sale in late 2017
A-EON's machines aren't the only PowerPC-based Amiga-compatibles. There were also the
Pegasos
,
Pegasos II
and
Efika 5200B
from Genesi, which ran a third-party AmigaOS-compatible OS called
MorphOS
. MorphOS is still around, and its latest version,
3.19
, came out in January. As well as Genesi kit,
MorphOS also supports
the AmigaOne 500 and Amiga X5000, plus several models of G4 and G5 Apple PowerMac (
The Reg
FOSS desk has an older version on a Mac mini G4).
AROS 1.2 for 68K, also in Amiga Forever. Not identical, but certainly very familiar
From the perspective of 2025, it looks like the Amiga world backed the wrong RISC-y horse with PowerPC. In hindsight, we wish they'd opted for Arm hardware instead. A Raspberry Pi 400 running an Arm-native Amiga-compatible OS would be great fun. For now, the next best thing for mass-market hardware is the
AROS Research Operating System
. This mainly targets x86 PC compatibles, although there's also a version for classic Amiga kit. There is a work-in-progress
Arm port
, but the current version works best hosted under Arm Linux. ®

43646362.article_summary: 2025年，比利时软件公司Hyperion Entertainment发布了AmigaOS 3.2的第三次更新（版本3.2.3），特别针对配备680x0处理器及PiStorm加速板的Amiga电脑。此次更新提升了色彩表现和分辨率。尽管更新时间不规律，但Hyperion对操作系统的持续投入值得肯定，尤其是公司在经历股东破产和所有权变更后依然坚持开发。此外，AmigaOS 4继续支持PowerPC处理器的Amiga设备，而第三方操作系统MorphOS也仍在更新。与此同时，AROS研发操作系统正开发Arm移植版本，目前在x86 PC上表现最佳。总体而言，Amiga社区在硬件选择上偏向PowerPC的决策受到质疑，但复古计算爱好者仍有许多选择。

---

争议焦点：旧操作系统更新的实际价值及其对资源分配的影响。一方认为更新对稳定性和安全性至关重要，另一方则认为资源应更多投入到新系统开发中。

data.title: How University Students Use Claude
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：学生使用AI（尤其是LLM如ChatGPT和Claude）在学业中的影响，包括作弊问题、学习过程的改变以及对教育的长期影响。

不同观点：
• **AI作弊问题广泛存在**：dtnewman认为，学生广泛使用AI来作弊，例如直接将作业粘贴到ChatGPT中获取答案，这削弱了学习过程。他指出，AI让学习变得过于容易，使得学生错过了通过挣扎和思考来真正掌握知识的机会。

• **AI对学习的深层次影响**：defgeneric强调，AI不仅会导致作弊问题，还可能破坏深度学习过程。他指出，学术学习需要通过挣扎和思考来内化知识，而AI的即时答案会阻碍这一过程，最终可能导致学生无法真正掌握知识。

• **AI公司有动机淡化作弊问题**：SamBam认为，Anthropic等AI公司有动机淡化学生使用AI写论文等作弊行为，因为他们可能会刻意模糊或掩盖这些问题的严重性。

• **AI使用数据需要更透明**：walleeee指出，虽然文章试图正面描述AI的使用，但数据表明许多学生使用AI直接获取答案，而非进行深度学习。这表明AI可能成为分化技术，而非普及教育的工具。

• **技术细节学习的重要性**：sebstefan对技术解释和解决方案被混在一起报告表示不满，认为理解底层技术细节对于学习至关重要。

• **AI对写作和思维的影响**：dagw和zebomon讨论了AI对写作和思维的影响。他们认为，写作是思维的体现，过度依赖AI写作可能导致学生失去思考和表达的能力。

• **如何避免AI对学习的负面影响**：moojacob作为学生，提出了如何避免在使用AI时阻碍学习的担忧，并分享了个人经验。他担心使用AI会让他错过通过犯错学习的宝贵机会。

• **AI作为学习工具的潜力**：pugio分享了积极使用AI进行自学的经验，认为AI可以作为强大的学习辅助工具，帮助学生更高效地掌握知识。

• **重新定义作弊和教育的意义**：_tom_提出，作弊的定义需要根据AI时代的现实进行调整。他认为，教育应该为学生准备面对一个充满AI的职业生涯，而不是坚持过时的教学方法。

• **多数学生使用AI避免学习**：karpour认为，尽管AI工具能够帮助学习，但大多数学生实际上用它来避免学习。

• **不同教育阶段和LLM提供商的影响差异**：bluehatbrit对不同LLM提供商和教育阶段的使用情况表示好奇，并分享了其妻子在英国中学教学中观察到的学生使用Snapchat LLM的案例。

补充讨论：
• **AI对未来职业的影响**：_tom_的观点引发了关于AI对未来职业和教育目标的影响的讨论，强调教育需要适应AI时代的变化。

• **AI在学习中的潜在正面作用**：ozarkerD分享了个人经历，认为AI可以激发好奇心，成为学生探索知识的强大工具。

争议焦点：
• **AI在教育中的角色**：一方认为AI是作弊工具，严重破坏学习过程；另一方则认为AI是强大的学习辅助工具，可以帮助学生更高效地学习。
• **作弊定义的改变**：是否应根据AI的普及重新定义作弊和教育的意义，以适应未来的职业需求。

data.title: How much do you think it costs to make a pair of Nike shoes in Asia?
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: 文章提到在x.com网站上，某些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展程序可能会导致问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展程序，然后重试访问网站。文章提醒用户不必担心，可以尝试再次操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：全球供应链与制造业成本分析，特别是中美之间的经济竞争与鞋类产品的生产和定价问题。

不同观点：
• **Rayiner**：认为美国需要正视中国在科技领域的崛起，尤其是在核能、AI、电动车和电池等领域。他预测中国在经济总量上将超过美国，并质疑美国未来的竞争优势。他担心美国可能会像如今的英国一样，在全球产业链中失去实际生产优势，仅保留金融和服务业的优势。

• **hx8**：质疑鞋类产品定价中的利润分配问题。他质疑为什么Footlocker在成本上升时需要提高利润，而不是保持固定的利润率，尤其是当运营成本（如广告和零售空间）是固定时。

• **TrapLord_Rhodo**：批评文章使用假设的鞋款价格作为依据，指出高端品牌鞋即使在中国制造，也能卖出高价，强调品牌效应在定价中的作用。

• **aimor**：试图通过具体数字分析鞋类产品在不同环节中的成本分配，特别是在加征关税后的成本变化，并提出美国制造商如何在成本上与进口产品竞争的问题。

• **ZeroGravitas**：引用喜剧歌曲讽刺低成本制造背后的道德问题，特别是使用廉价劳动力的现象，质疑为何消费者仍需支付较高价格。

• **phkahler**：对供应链中各环节的百分比加价模式提出疑问，不理解为何每个环节都需要按成本百分比加价，而不是固定利润。

• **hnburnsy**：指出文章中对Footlocker的折扣计算存在模糊，认为实际销售价格和财务报告中的数字不一致，并讨论零售商和品牌自营店的不同成本结构。

• **ctrlp**：从消费者角度出发，关注鞋子的耐用性和长期使用成本，而不是仅仅看购买价格，质疑低价鞋的质量和使用寿命。

• **raincom**：分享在零售业工作的负面经验，质疑美国应创造什么样的工作岗位，是低质量的零售工作还是制造业工作。

• **jimt1234**：对特定类型鞋子（如Crocs）的制造成本提出疑问，认为其成本应非常低，因其生产工艺简单。

• **subsubzero**：通过历史价格对比，指出Nike通过外包和供应链效率降低产品价格，同时分析赞助和市场营销对最终售价的影响，建议通过提高售价或减少赞助费来促进美国制造业回流。

• **ZiiS**：认为文章使用了一些夸张手法，指出Nike等品牌的大部分利润用于广告和赞助，并认为市场需求会决定生产技术和成本的变化。

• **ForOldHack**：质疑文章中关于亚洲工人待遇的统计数据，基于自身经历指出实际工资水平远低于报道，并认为文章缺乏对现实的准确反映。

• **ungreased0675**：指出实际市场中亚洲制造的鞋子售价接近美国制造的鞋子，强调产品在价值链中的巨大加价现象。

补充讨论：
- 文章和评论中多次提到品牌效应、市场营销和赞助费用对最终产品价格的影响，特别是在高端鞋类市场中。
- 多个评论关注美国和中国在制造业和科技领域的竞争，以及未来全球经济格局的变化。
- 对供应链各环节的成本分配和利润加成模式存在较大争议，特别是各环节的定价逻辑和实际成本结构。

data.title: Tech CEO: 4-day work week didn't hurt or help productivity
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: Civo的CEO马克·博斯特（Mark Boost）接受采访时表示，公司自2021年起实施四天工作制，虽然生产力没有明显提升或下降，但员工反馈积极，有助于吸引和留住人才。员工大多选择周五休息，获得三天的周末，以便处理个人事务。然而，销售和客服等部门因需要五日覆盖，面临一定挑战，通过增加人手解决。尽管微软和戴尔曾试验四天工作制并取得积极成果，但未广泛推行。总体来看，四天工作制在科技行业中仍存在实施难度，但员工满意度显著提升。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：四天工作制与五天工作制的效率对比

不同观点：
• 观点一：四天工作制显示了五天工作制中存在大量冗余时间。如果四天工作制能够维持同样的产出，意味着在五天工作制中，员工并没有充分利用所有的工作时间。这暗示了员工在当前的工作周中可能存在低效或时间浪费的情况。（支持方：mytailorisrich）
    └─ 论据或例子：通过转向四天工作制可以揭示五天工作制中的低效率问题。

• 观点二：四天工作制可能提高了工作效率。因为员工在更短的工作周内必须更加专注和高效，以完成相同的工作量，这可能促使人们减少拖延和分心。（隐含观点：四天工作制可以激励更高的生产力）
    └─ 论据或例子：较短的工作周可能迫使员工优化时间管理，从而提升整体效率。

• 观点三：工作产出不能单纯通过工作天数来衡量。有些人认为工作的质量和产出与工作时间长短并非线性相关，而与员工的工作状态、任务复杂性等因素有关。因此，转向四天工作制不一定会减少产出，反而可能增加员工的幸福感和工作满意度。（支持方：可能反对单纯关注时间长短的人）
    └─ 论据或例子：四天工作制可能提高员工幸福感，从而间接提高工作效率和质量。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：四天工作制是否真的能保持与五天工作制相同的工作产出，以及是否存在冗余时间是讨论的核心。一部分人认为它揭示了五天工作制的低效，而另一部分人则认为四天工作制能激励更高的效率和工作满意度。
  
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：评论中隐含了对工作效率和员工幸福感之间关系的思考，四天工作制可能不仅仅是减少工作时间，还涉及整体工作生活质量的提升。

Tech CEO: 4-day work week didn't hurt or help productivity
6
'There are challenges' but staff recruitment and retention isn't one of them
Paul Kunert
Thu 10 Apr 2025
//
11:57 UTC
Interview
Civo shifted its workforce to a four-day working week and while it hasn't changed productivity much at the cloud biz, it has helped attract "new talent" and retain existing staff, CEO Mark Boost says.
While Microsoft and Dell would prefer to keep quiet about work-life balance programs embarked upon during 2019 and 2022 respectively, others in the tech industry – albeit of a different scale – are embracing change.
"We piloted the four-day week in 2020 and after a successful pilot, which included gathering feedback from our staff, we decided to implement it in January 2021, so we're now four years on from adopting full time," he tells
The Register
.
"During our original pilot we saw no decline in productivity (I wouldn't say we had any gain). However, the feedback was super positive and staff liked the extra day off and felt they had a much better work-life balance.
"Every employee is on a four-day week and most employees opted for Fridays off, which gives them a three-day weekend and I know many employees have said it allows them an opportunity on a Friday to catch-up on personal tasks/admin, allowing them more freedom on Saturday/Sunday."
Brit consultancy 4 Day Week Foundation last month launched a campaign to get more local
tech businesses to adopt new working styles
. It is starting trials for the latest batch of entrants from the end of June.
Is this out of sync with an industry better known for pushing people hard to work long hours? Google co-founder Sergey Brin recently said he wanted AI engineers in the office at least five days a week,
working 60-plus hour weeks
.
"It's also been great for us to attract new talent and has helped us retain talent. We didn't need a restructure at all, but in certain roles we need coverage on Fridays and often weekends too (e.g. customer support), so we have to flex time and ensure we have enough rotation to ensure we have enough coverage," says Boost.
Everyone at Civo does their full week's hours during the four days. While it may be good for the staff, is it a headache for management?
"The four-day week does present some challenges across certain departments, e.g. sales and customer support where we need coverage beyond four days, but we've been able to work around this by hiring extra people to improve our coverage."
91% of polled Amazon staff unhappy with return-to-office, 3-in-4 want to jump ship
Results are in for biggest 4-day work week trial ever: 92% sticking with it
Next six months could set a new pace for work-life balance
Most Londoners would quit before they give up working from home
Despite its reluctance to talk to
The Reg
about why it hasn't expanded its own initiative, Microsoft said in 2019 that its trial of a four-day week in Japan made for happier staff, more efficient meetings, and a 40 percent increased productivity rate.
"Work a short time, rest well, and learn a lot,"
Microsoft Japan president and CEO Takuya Hirano said
at the time. "I want employees to think about and experience how they can achieve the same results with 20 percent less working time."
The added bonus was also lower operating costs in terms of electricity and printed pages. In these times of Microsoft spending big on AI datacenters, eking out efficiencies make more sense. We previously asked Microsoft why it hasn't rolled out the scheme to more offices across the world.
A spokesperson told us they'd look into our inquiry and "let you know if we have anything to add." Since then? Crickets.
Dell is the same. Staff seemingly loved the four-day week but it didn't expand beyond
tests in the Netherlands and Argentina
. Dell didn't respond to requests for comment.
Maybe it's investor anxiety. Or maybe tech's billionaire class still prefers the go-hard-or-go-home ethos. ®
